# Hectare Mini — Firmware 2.2.8

# What the Hectare Mini system does

The seeding control system with the Hectare Mini panel is made by Agriwelt GmbH. It watches sowing and fertilizing on seed drills and planters of any make, in real time, and on machines with electric dispenser motors it also drives the metering so that the set rate is applied.

The panel sits in the cab: a 320 × 240 colour screen and seven touch buttons around it — see [The panel and its seven buttons](front-panel.md). Everything else is on the machine: one sensor per seed line, and whatever the machine needs besides.

## Seed

- Shows the seed flow in every seed line, live, as a column on the [section diagram](section-diagram.md).
- Raises an alarm when the flow in a line falls off or stops, **with the number of the line**.
- Compares the seeding with the target rate the operator sets (the **“Hybrid”** and **“Precise”** modes) and raises an alarm when it deviates more than allowed.
- Counts seeds, **doubles and skips** at every coulter (the **“Precise”** mode).
- Splits the treated area into the area sown and the area not sown.

## Fertilizer

- Shows the flow of dry fertilizer in every line and raises an alarm, by line number, when it falls off or stops.
- Watches liquid fertilizer lines, where the machine has them.

## The machine around the seed

- Hopper level, dispenser shaft rotation, fan speed, air pressure at the fan outlet, travel speed — each against its own limits.
- Optional: the shaft speed against the travel speed, and the weight of seed applied by the dispensers.
- Working or transport position of the drill.
- The sensors of a separate fan-drive engine — oil pressure, battery charge, ignition, fuel level, air filter. They are optional and meant for drill combinations with their own diesel engine.

## Driving the metering and the tramline

- On machines with electric dispenser motors: applies up to three products to the rate in kg/ha, or the seed to the rate in seeds per metre — see [The rate control screen](rate-control-screen.md) and [The Motors screen](motors-screen.md).
- Makes tramlines with tramline actuators or by stopping motors — see [Set up the tramline rhythm](tramline-rhythm.md).

## Speed

The travel speed comes from a wheel or radar sensor, or from the GPS receiver built into the panel. When GPS is set up, it is used while it has a valid fix, and the sensor takes over by itself when it loses the signal — see [GPS reception](gps-receiver.md).

## Records

Detailed statistics for each field, kept over switch-off — see [The Statistics screen](statistics-screen.md).

## Contact

Agriwelt GmbH · Hackhofergasse 1 · 1190 Wien, Austria · phone +43 664 156 4910 · info@agriwelt.com · www.agriwelt.com. This is also the address wherever this manual sends you to the technical service.

> **SEE ALSO**
>
> [Quick start](quick-start.md) · [Commissioning](commissioning.md) · [Terms](terms.md)


# The panel and its seven buttons

The Hectare Mini panel has a 320 × 240 colour screen and seven buttons on the frame around it. The buttons are touch areas, not mechanical keys: a short touch is a short press; a touch held for about half a second is a long press.

::: {.anatomy fig="panel-callouts"}
1. **Power button.** Touch-sensitive, at the top edge of the housing.
2. **Bracket.** Lets you mount the panel on a flat surface at any angle, horizontally or vertically. For mounting on a tube, an additional bracket is available.
3. **The seven buttons.** Three on the left, three on the right, one under the screen — see the table below.
4. **Screen.** It also takes touches in some places, for example the digits of the [number pad](number-pad.md).
5. **Cable entry.** One harness brings the speed sensor, the sensor network and the power supply to the panel.

The panel from the front and from the side, and its harness.
:::

## The seven buttons

| **Button** | **Short press** | **Long press** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![](figures/icons/key-home.png){height=34px} **“HOME”** | Moves on to the next working screen. In an alarm window: closes the alarm. | On the home screen and the rate control screen: locks or unlocks product application, if the machine has dispenser motors or a liquid fertilizer pump. In an alarm window: closes it and returns to the home screen. |
| ![](figures/icons/key-back.png){height=34px} **“BACK”** | Leaves a menu, a window or a mode, one step back. On the home screen: opens the tramline bout menu, if the tramline is on. | On the home screen, while seeding: sets the alarm level from the flow being applied — see [Set the alarm level](set-the-alarm-level.md). |
| ![](figures/icons/key-minus.png){height=34px} **“MINUS”** | Lowers the selected value. In the sensor setup mode: takes the selected sensor out of control. | — |
| ![](figures/icons/key-menu.png){height=34px} **“MENU”** | Opens the menu of the screen, or enters the selected menu item. In the sensor setup mode: opens the context menu of the selected device. | On the home screen, the rate control screen and the Motors screen: switches on the sensor setup mode. |
| ![](figures/icons/key-plus.png){height=34px} **“PLUS”** | Raises the selected value. In the sensor setup mode: takes the selected sensor into control. | — |
| ![](figures/icons/key-down.png){height=34px} **“DOWN”** | Selects the next item, field or device. | — |
| ![](figures/icons/key-up.png){height=34px} **“UP”** | Selects the previous item, field or device. | — |

> **NOTE**
>
> **Holding a button does not repeat it.** One touch is one step, however long you hold it — a held button either does its long-press function or nothing. To change a value by ten steps, touch ten times. Where a value is large, the [number pad](number-pad.md) is quicker.

If **“Buttons sound”** is set to **“Yes”** in the [Settings menu](settings-menu.md), the panel beeps at every touch it accepts.

What every button does on every screen: [Buttons on every screen](buttons-and-gestures.md).


# Switching on and off

After the power is switched on, a splash screen with the logo appears. It stays until the panel has found every device connected to it — a few seconds — and then the panel changes to its first working screen.

![The splash screen with the logo.](figures/splash)

The logo on the splash screen depends on the supplier of the system and may differ from the picture.

> **NOTE**
>
> **If the splash screen stays much longer than usual,** the panel is waiting for a device that does not answer. Look at the alarms as soon as the working screen appears — see [How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md).

## What state the panel starts in

- **Access level: Operator.** After every power-on the panel is at the Operator level, whatever level was set before. Operator is the only level at which alarm windows are shown, so switching off and on is also the quickest way back to safe working. See [Access levels](access-levels.md).
- **The home screen** — with one exception: if the [rate control screen](rate-control-screen.md) was open when the panel was switched off, it opens again. It is the only screen the panel remembers.
- **Work paused, on a bench.** If speed imitation is switched on and the machine has dispenser motors, the panel starts with product application locked — see [Lock application by hand](lock-application-by-hand.md).

The version of the software, the serial number of the panel and its hardware identifier can be read at any time: press **“MENU”** on the home screen and choose the last item of the main menu. **“BACK”** or **“Close”** leaves the window.

## Switching off

| **What** | **When it is written** |
| --- | --- |
| Settings, target rates, alarm levels | By themselves, about one and a half seconds after the last change and the last touch of a button. |
| [Statistics](statistics-screen.md) of the active field | Every five minutes, and a few seconds after the machine stops. |
| Readings of the [Seeding table](table-screen.md) | Never — they belong to the working session and start from zero after every power-on. |

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **Stop before you switch off, and wait a few seconds.** Otherwise the last stretch of work is missing from the statistics, and a value changed just before may not be stored.


# Screens, menus, context menus and windows

Everything on the panel happens through the **working screens**, the **menus**, the **context menu** of a device and the **windows** that ask or tell you something. Numbers are typed on the [number pad](number-pad.md).

## The working screens

**“HOME”** moves on from one working screen to the next, always in this order:

| **Screen** | **Shown** |
| --- | --- |
| [Home screen](home-screen.md) | Always. |
| [Seeding table](table-screen.md) | Always. |
| [Statistics](statistics-screen.md) | Always. |
| [Motors](motors-screen.md) | Only if the machine has dispenser motors or tramline actuators, and only above the Operator access level. |
| [Rate control](rate-control-screen.md) | Always. One more **“HOME”** returns to the home screen. |

**“BACK”** returns to the home screen from the Seeding table, the Statistics and the Motors screen. The rate control screen is left only with **“HOME”**.

![The home screen and the Statistics screen, two of the working screens.](figures/screens-cycle)

## Menus

**“MENU”** opens the menu of the screen you are on — on the home screen, the main menu.

::: {.anatomy fig="menu-look"}
1. **Selected item.** Black text on a blue band. **“UP”** and **“DOWN”** move the band; at the end of the list it jumps to the other end.
2. **Value between − and +.** Shown on the selected item: change it with **“PLUS”** and **“MINUS”**, right there in the list.
3. **Value of an item that is not selected.** The − and + appear when you select it.
4. **Arrow head.** The item opens another menu. Press **“MENU”**.
5. **Scroll bar.** The list is longer than the screen.

The **“Settings”** menu, with **“Language”** selected.
:::

| **What you see on the right** | **What it does** |
| --- | --- |
| An arrow head | Opens another menu. Press **“MENU”**. |
| A value between **-** and **+** | **“PLUS”** and **“MINUS”** change it one step at a time. |
| A value between **-\[** and **\]+** | **“PLUS”** and **“MINUS”** change it one step at a time; **“MENU”** opens the [number pad](number-pad.md) to type it. |
| Nothing | The item performs an action. Press **“MENU”**. |

You can also touch an item to select it and touch it again to open it. **“BACK”** leaves a menu, one level up.

## The context menu of a device

Every sensor on the home screen, the rate control screen and the Motors screen has its own menu. Hold **“MENU”** until one device is shown on a white background — this is the **sensor setup mode** — then select the device with **“UP”** and **“DOWN”** and press **“MENU”**. How to work in this mode: [Take a sensor into or out of control](sensor-in-and-out-of-control.md). The items of each context menu are in [Sensor settings](sensor-settings.md).

![The context menu of the speed sensor.](figures/ctx-speed)

## Windows that ask, and windows that tell

A **question window** has a yellow strip with **“Confirmation”**. The lines under the question name the two buttons that answer it — they differ from window to window, so read them. The green **“Yes”** and red **“No”** on the screen can also be touched. **“BACK”**, or a touch outside the window, always cancels.

![A question window: here PLUS answers Yes and MINUS answers No.](figures/question-window)

An **information window** has a blue strip with **“Information”**. It closes by itself, or with a touch or a button.

## Alarm windows

::: {.anatomy fig="alarm-window"}
1. **Red strip.** **“FAILURE!”** — the window reports a fault.
2. **Hint.** **“HOME”** closes the window.
3. **The fault.** Here the connection to a sensor is lost.
4. **Type of the sensor.** Here the fan.
5. **Numbers of the sensors.** When several sensors of the same type have the same fault, all their numbers are listed.
6. **“Close”.** Touch it to close the window.

An alarm window about the fan sensor.
:::

While the window is shown, the panel sounds the alarm signal and lights its alarm indicator. **“HOME”** or a touch of **“Close”** closes the window; **“HOME”** held closes it and returns to the home screen. The other buttons do nothing here. All alarms and what to do: [How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md).

## Access levels

| **Level** | **What it opens** |
| --- | --- |
| **“Operator”** | What you need for work. Active after every power-on. The only level at which alarm windows are shown. |
| **“Agronomist”** | Hidden items and parameters of the machine and the sensors. Needs a code from the data sheet of your panel. |
| **“Service”** | The profile and the rest of the commissioning work — for the service only. The configuration of seed and pressure sensors needs only the **“Agronomist”** level. |

The level is chosen in **“Settings”** → **“User”**. How: [Enable the Agronomist level](enable-agronomist-level.md). In this manual, a parameter that needs a higher level says so.


# The number pad

Some values can be typed as a whole number instead of being stepped with **“PLUS”** and **“MINUS”**. In a menu such a value stands between **-\[** and **\]+**; press **“MENU”** on it and the number pad opens. The pad also opens by itself where steps make no sense — for the weight at the end of a [motor calibration](calibrate-motor-weight.md), for the number of holes in the disk of a [dispenser motor](motor-context-menu.md), and for an access code.

![The item Width, cm in a menu and the number pad it opens.](figures/mini-keypad-width)

## What the pad shows

::: {.anatomy fig="mini-keypad-parts"}
1. **Name of the parameter**, in light blue. In some windows the whole prompt, over several lines.
2. **The number.** It opens with the present value (empty if the value is 0) and grows to the left as you type.
3. **Backspace.** A touch deletes the last character; touch and hold deletes the whole number.
4. **Digits.** Touch them — the digits are typed on the screen only.
5. **.− key.** Sets the decimal point. Touch and hold switches the minus sign, where the value may be negative.
6. **“OK”**, in green. Accepts the number and closes the pad.

The number pad for the working width.
:::

A touched key does not light up. You see that the touch has arrived by the number, and you hear it if the button sound is on.

## Typing a number

::: steps
1. On a menu item whose value stands between **-\[** and **\]+**, press **“MENU”**. The pad opens.

2. Touch and hold the backspace. The old value is cleared.

3. Touch the digits. Each joins the number on the right.

4. If the value has tenths, touch **.−** and type the places after the point.

5. Check the number, then touch **“OK”** or press **“MENU”**. The pad closes and the menu shows the new value.
:::

**“BACK”** leaves the pad without changing anything. The other buttons and a touch outside the keys do nothing.

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **The panel does not warn you.** A number outside the permitted range is silently replaced by the nearest limit — for **“Width, cm”** a typed 50 becomes 100. An **empty field is accepted as 0**, not as the smallest permitted value. If you have cleared the field by mistake, press **“BACK”** and open the pad again.

## Rules of the pad

- **The point works only where the value has tenths**, for example **“Minimum, rpm”** and **“Maximum, rpm”** of a dispenser motor. For whole numbers the **.−** key does nothing.
- **One point per number.** A second touch of **.−** does nothing until you delete the first point.
- **The places after the point are limited** to what the value knows. Type fewer and the panel adds zeros: with one place, 12 becomes 12.0.
- **The length is limited** by the width of the field. When it is full, further digits do nothing.


# Quick start — before and during the first pass

This assumes the system has been commissioned — see [Commissioning](commissioning.md). Before the season the speed sensor must have been calibrated, and the dispensers too if their shaft speed or the seed weight is to be watched ([Speed sensor](speed-sensor.md), [Sensor settings](sensor-settings.md)).

## Before the field

::: steps
1. Switch the panel on and wait for the home screen.

2. Press **“HOME”** twice to open the Statistics screen. Check that the right **active field** is selected; on a new field, select an empty one or erase it — [Start a new field](start-a-new-field.md).

3. Back on the home screen, set the **alarm level** of the seed diagram with **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”** — or, in the **“Hybrid”** and **“Precise”** modes, the **target rate**. **“DOWN”** moves to the fertilizer diagram. See [Change the target rate](set-the-target-rate.md).

   ![The seed diagram with the alarm level in s/s and its control line.](figures/diagram-threshold)

4. If products are applied by weight, set their rates in kg/ha the same way.

5. Check the settings that change with the work — in the sensor setup mode ([Take a sensor into or out of control](sensor-in-and-out-of-control.md)), each sensor separately: **“Period, s”** of each dispenser shaft sensor; **“Minimum, rpm”** and **“Maximum, rpm”** of each fan; **“Minimum, Pa”** and **“Maximum, Pa”** of each pressure sensor; **“Fraction”** and **“Correction”** of the seed sensors and of the fertilizer sensors. All seed sensors share one set of settings, all fertilizer sensors another; every other sensor has its own.

6. Make sure the access level is **“Operator”**. At a higher level no alarm windows are shown, and the panel warns you with an alarm if you start seeding. Switching off and on returns to Operator.
:::

## Seeding

Just start. There is nothing to switch on: the panel starts watching the alarms by itself, with **one short beep**, once these conditions have held for the **“Alarm delay”** (3 s by default):

- application is not locked by hand ([Lock application by hand](lock-application-by-hand.md));
- with an implement position sensor under control: the drill is in the working position;
- with dispenser motors or a liquid pump: the drill moves, and the speed sensor is under control and shows a speed;
- otherwise: at least **“Percent of sowing,%”** (20 % by default) of the lines under control are sowing — and, with **“Seeding criteria”** set at the speed sensor, the drill moves.

When a condition fails, the watching stops at once with **three short beeps**. There is no separate alarm for a drill that moves while no seed arrives: then the watching does not start and the beep does not come.

![The home screen during work.](figures/home-at-work)

## During the first pass, check

- the **speed** against the tractor's speedometer or a GPS navigator;
- the **fan speed** and the **pressure** — within their limits, not red;
- the **seed columns** above their line, and the seed rate against the target in the **“Hybrid”** and **“Precise”** modes;
- the **fertilizer columns** above their line;
- the **product rate** in kg/ha against the target;
- no red on any other indicator — [Indicators](indicators.md).

If the speed sensor fails, the speed can be imitated in its settings until it is repaired ([Speed sensor](speed-sensor.md)). When an alarm appears, stop and clear the fault — [How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md). The quality of the last stretch is on the [Seeding table](table-screen.md); the result for the whole field on the [Statistics screen](statistics-screen.md).


# Commissioning — setting up a new system

This is the sequence for the dealer or service engineer when the system is installed. Each step links to the topic with the details. Most of the parameters need the **Agronomist** access level — [Enable the Agronomist level](enable-agronomist-level.md).

::: steps
1. **Connect** all devices to the panel and check their power supply according to the wiring diagram in the data sheet of the system.

2. **Check the profile.** It must match the equipment of the machine — [The profile](profile.md). If it does not, set it up first.

3. **Check the connections.** Every sensor must answer and be under control — see [Indicators](indicators.md) for the red cross and the not-controlled sign.

4. **Set the general parameters** in **“Settings”** → **“Seeding machine parameters”** ([Settings menu](settings-menu.md)):
   the working width, **“Width, cm”**; **“Mode of seeding”** — **“Flow”** for a grain drill; **“Mode of fertilizers”** — **“Flow”**.

5. **Set the sensors** ([Sensor settings](sensor-settings.md)):
   - speed sensor: **“Diameter, cm”** and **“Pulses”**; **“Imitation, km/h”** at **“No”**; then the speed calibration;
   - dispenser shaft sensors: **“Period, s”**; if wanted, **“Rotation speed control”** or **“Weight control”**, each followed by its calibration;
   - fans: **“Pulses”**, **“Minimum, rpm”**, **“Maximum, rpm”**;
   - pressure sensors: **“Filter”**, **“Minimum, Pa”**, **“Maximum, Pa”**;
   - implement position sensor: **“Transporting position signal”**;
   - engine sensors: **“Activation signal”**;
   - seed sensors, and separately fertilizer sensors: at least **“Fraction”** for the crop.

6. **Set up the tramline**, if the machine makes tramlines — after the profile, never before: [Set up the tramline rhythm](tramline-rhythm.md).

7. **On machines with dispenser motors:** assign the products and calibrate every motor — [Assign a product to a motor](assign-product-to-motor.md), [Calibrate a motor by weight](calibrate-motor-weight.md).
:::

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **The panel stores a change by itself** about one and a half seconds after the last change and the last touch of a button. Wait a few seconds before switching off.

Each sensor is set separately — except the seed sensors, which share one set of settings, and the fertilizer sensors, which share another.

When everything is set, return to the **“Operator”** level (switching off and on does it) and go to [Quick start](quick-start.md).


# About this manual and its pictures

## How to read this manual

- **NOTE** — extra information, for example a capability you may not know of.
- **IMPORTANT**, **CAUTION**, **WARNING** — information that costs work, a crop or a part if you ignore it.
- A parameter that is visible only above the **“Operator”** level says so — see [Access levels](access-levels.md).
- **Press** means a short touch of a button; **hold** means a touch held until the panel reacts, about half a second.
- Labels in quotes, such as **“Settings”**, are written exactly as the English panel shows them.

## The pictures

The screens are real frames from a Hectare Mini panel with firmware 2.2.8, mostly shot on a test bench instead of a machine in the field. Some belong to an earlier firmware; where the layout differs, the text describes 2.2.8. A few things in them belong to the bench:

| **What you see in a picture** | **Why it is there** | **What your panel shows instead** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A blue hours:minutes in the clock slot, or **TRIAL** | The bench panel runs on a trial licence. | The time of day — see [Clock](indicators.md#clock). |
| Yellow **IMITAT** in the clock slot | The bench runs in an imitation mode. | The time of day. |
| A yellow speed figure, or **IMITATION** | The speed is imitated — no wheel turns on a bench. | The measured speed in white. |
| Red hoppers, red dispenser shafts, a red fan with **XXXX** | The bench has no product, no shafts turning and no fan connected. | Grey indicators while everything is in order. |
| Zeros on the Statistics screen and the Seeding table | The bench was standing still. | Your figures. |

Where an English picture is still missing, the page shows "Picture to follow"; the text says everything the picture would show. The German pages show the German frame in its place.

> **NOTE**
>
> The question, information and alarm windows were brought to one shape with a coloured strip across the top in firmware 2.2.8: yellow for a question, blue for information, red for a fault.


# The home screen

The home screen is the main working screen. It shows the state of every device of the machine and, below, one diagram for the seed and one for the fertilizer. What it shows follows the [profile](profile.md): every device entered there gets its indicator. When space runs short, the panel makes the speed figure or the diagrams smaller, and on a crowded screen it leaves out the area or the population indicator.

## A planter with seed and fertilizer

::: {.anatomy fig="home-elements"}
1. **Travel speed**, in km/h. Messages about the speed replace the figure. [Speed](indicators.md#speed)
2. **Hoppers**, numbered. Red — empty. [Hopper](indicators.md#hopper)
3. **Dispenser shafts.** Grey — in order; the icon turns while the shaft turns. [Dispenser shaft](indicators.md#dispenser-shaft)
4. **Clock.** The time of day; it also carries messages. [Clock](indicators.md#clock)
5. **Markers.** Yellow — both marker arms are up. [Markers](indicators.md#markers)
6. **Fan** and its speed in rpm. [Fan](indicators.md#fan)
7. **Area** treated on the active field, in ha. [Area](indicators.md#area)
8. **Population** — the seeding density in thousands of seeds per hectare, in the **“Precise”** mode. [Population](indicators.md#population)
9. **Seed diagram.** One column per seed sensor. [The section diagram](section-diagram.md)
10. **Scale of skips and doubles**, in per cent (**“Precise”** mode).
11. **Seed rate field.** Measured rate on top, target below, here in seeds per metre. [Change the target rate](set-the-target-rate.md)
12. **Section numbers.**
13. **Fertilizer diagram**, here in the **“Flow”** mode, with its control line.
14. **Fertilizer rate field.** Measured flow on top, alarm level below, in fertilizer units per second.

A 12-row planter in the “Precise” mode with 12 fertilizer lines in the “Flow” mode, standing still.
:::

## A grain drill on the bench

::: {.anatomy fig="home-idle"}
1. **Travel speed.**
2. **Hoppers.** Red outline — empty.
3. **Dispenser shafts.** Red — alarm: the shaft does not turn.
4. **Clock.**
5. **Fan.** Red with **XXXX** — no connection to the fan sensor.
6. **Area.**
7. **GPS reception.** The satellite icon and the number of satellites used. [GPS reception](gps-receiver.md)
8. **Seed column.** Dark grey — no flow, the drill stands.
9. **Control line.** The alarm level drawn across the diagram.
10. **Rate field.** Measured flow on top, alarm level below, in seeds per second.
11. **Section numbers.**

A 12-row grain drill in the “Flow” mode, standing still on the bench with no product and no fan.
:::

All indicators and their states: [Indicators](indicators.md). The diagram — columns, lines, colours: [The section diagram](section-diagram.md).

## Two modes

The home screen works in two modes:

- **Monitoring mode** — after switch-on. You watch the work and change the rates.
- **Sensor setup mode** — hold **“MENU”**. One device is shown on a white background; **“UP”** and **“DOWN”** move to the next device, **“PLUS”** and **“MINUS”** take it into or out of control, **“MENU”** opens its context menu. **“BACK”** leaves the mode. See [Take a sensor into or out of control](sensor-in-and-out-of-control.md).

![The home screen in the sensor setup mode: the speed indicator is selected.](figures/sensor-mode-enter)

## What you can do from the home screen

| **To do this** | **Do this** |
| --- | --- |
| Open the main menu | **“MENU”** |
| Change a target rate or alarm level | **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”**; **“UP”** / **“DOWN”** choose the field — [Change the target rate](set-the-target-rate.md) |
| Let the panel set the alarm level | Hold **“BACK”** while seeding — [Set the alarm level](set-the-alarm-level.md) |
| Lock or unlock product application | Hold **“HOME”** — [Lock application by hand](lock-application-by-hand.md) |
| Open the tramline bout menu | **“BACK”** — [Next tramline bout](next-tramline-bout.md) |
| Open the settings of a device | Hold **“MENU”**, select it, **“MENU”** |
| Go to the next working screen | **“HOME”** — [Screens, menus and windows](interface-basics.md) |


# Indicators of the home screen and their states

Read the indicators by colour. On firmware 2.2.8 a device in order is drawn in **grey**; **red**, mostly blinking, is an alarm; **yellow** is a state you should know about but not a fault. Three states are the same for every sensor:

| **What you see** | **Meaning** | **What to do** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![](figures/icons/no-connection.png){height=32px} A red cross, blinking, or **XXXX** in place of the value | No connection to the sensor. | Check its cable and connectors. |
| A red question mark, blinking, or **????** in place of the value | A device of another type answers at this place. | Have the configuration checked by the service. |
| A grey not-controlled sign, blinking, or **!!!!** in place of the value | The sensor is taken out of control. It is not watched. | [Take it back into control](sensor-in-and-out-of-control.md) when the fault is repaired. |

## Speed

| **What you see** | **Meaning** |
| --- | --- |
| ![](figures/icons/speed-ok.png){height=32px} | The travel speed in km/h. |
| ![](figures/icons/speed-high.png){height=32px} alternating with ![](figures/icons/speed-slower.png){height=32px} | Faster than allowed. The red figure alternates with **“SLOWER”**. |
| ![](figures/icons/speed-low.png){height=32px} alternating with ![](figures/icons/speed-faster.png){height=32px} | Slower than allowed. The red figure alternates with **“FASTER”**. |
| Red figure alternating with **“Sensor”** 1 or 2, or with **“Settings”** | One of the two wheel sensors has failed, or the speed limits are set wrongly. |
| ![](figures/icons/speed-lost.png){height=32px} | No connection to the speed sensor. |
| ![](figures/icons/speed-sim-value.png){height=32px} alternating with ![](figures/icons/speed-simulation.png){height=32px} | Speed imitation is on: the figure is yellow and alternates with **“IMITATION”**. Outside the limits, with **INCREASE IMITATION** or **DECREASE IMITATION**. |

The speed is watched against its limits only if that control is switched on in the [speed sensor settings](speed-sensor.md). Where the speed comes from GPS: [GPS reception](gps-receiver.md).

## Hopper

| **What you see** | **Meaning** |
| --- | --- |
| Grey | Product above the sensor. |
| ![](figures/icons/hopper-empty.png){height=32px} red, blinking | The hopper is empty. |

## Dispenser shaft

| **What you see** | **Meaning** |
| --- | --- |
| Grey; turning while the shaft turns | In order. |
| ![](figures/icons/dispenser-alarm.png){height=32px} red, blinking | The shaft does not turn, or not at the speed required. |

## Fan

| **What you see** | **Meaning** |
| --- | --- |
| Grey, with the speed in rpm | In order. |
| Red, blinking, with the speed | The fan speed is outside its limits. |

## Pressure

| **What you see** | **Meaning** |
| --- | --- |
| Grey, with the pressure in kPa | In order. |
| ![](figures/icons/pressure-alarm.png){height=32px} red | The pressure at the fan outlet is outside its limits. |

## Engine sensors

The sensors of a separate fan-drive engine. Oil pressure and battery charge are watched only while the ignition is on.

| **What you see** | **Meaning** |
| --- | --- |
| ![](figures/icons/oil-alarm.png){height=32px} red | Low oil pressure. |
| ![](figures/icons/battery-alarm.png){height=32px} red | The battery is not charging. |
| ![](figures/icons/fuel-alarm.png){height=32px} red | Little fuel in the tank. |
| ![](figures/icons/airfilter-alarm.png){height=32px} red | The air filter is clogged. |
| Key grey / ![](figures/icons/ignition-off.png){height=32px} key yellow | Ignition on / ignition off. |

In order, each of these icons is grey.

## Implement position

| **What you see** | **Meaning** |
| --- | --- |
| Grey | The drill is in the working position. |
| ![](figures/icons/workpos-transport.png){height=32px} yellow, blinking | The drill is in the transport position. |

## Markers

Grey arms show which marker is down and which is up. With two marker sensors, both arms **yellow** means both markers are up.

## Tramline bout

Wheel tracks with the current bout on top and the number of bouts below — see [Next tramline bout](next-tramline-bout.md).

## Clock

| **What you see** | **Meaning** |
| --- | --- |
| White time | The time of day. |
| Red time, with a red **BAT** for a moment every four seconds | The clock battery must be replaced. |
| Red **XX:XX**, blinking | The clock is faulty. |
| Yellow **IMITAT** | The panel runs in an imitation mode — see [About the pictures](about-the-pictures.md). |
| Blue hours:minutes and **TRIAL** | A trial period is active: the time left. It appears every 30 seconds and covers the hopper and shaft icons for a moment. |

## Area

Hectares treated on the active field — shown only with a speed sensor, and only where the screen has room.

## Population

In the **“Precise”** mode: thousands of seeds per hectare, averaged over the seed sensors under control that answer. If seed and fertilizer are both in **“Precise”**, two indicators show, marked **A** (seed) and **B** (fertilizer); the area is then usually not shown.

## Product rate

One indicator per product applied by weight, with the product number, in kg/ha. Red and blinking: the rate deviates more than **“Product rate error,%”**. While it is within the tolerance, the panel shows the **target** figure.

## The column on the right

| **What you see** | **Meaning** |
| --- | --- |
| Motor symbol, yellow, blinking | Product application is locked by hand — see [Lock application by hand](lock-application-by-hand.md). |
| Actuator symbol, red, blinking | A dispenser motor or a tramline actuator is in alarm — see the [Motors screen](motors-screen.md). |
| Actuator symbol alternating with the not-controlled sign | A motor or an actuator is taken out of control. |
| Product symbol, red, blinking | The set rates cannot be applied at any speed — see [Calibrate a motor by weight](calibrate-motor-weight.md). |


# The section diagram — columns, lines and colours

Each column of a diagram is one seed or fertilizer line — one sensor. Its height is the flow through that line now. Next to the columns, the **rate field** shows the measured rate on top and the set value below it; while you change the set value it turns yellow for a few seconds. How the rest is drawn depends on the mode set in **“Mode of seeding”** and **“Mode of fertilizers”**: **“Flow”**, **“Hybrid”** or **“Precise”**. The fertilizer diagram always stands above the seed diagram and is usually run in **“Flow”**.

## “Flow” mode

![The seed diagram in the Flow mode with its marks.](figures/diagram-flow)

- **Alarm level** — the lower figure of the rate field, in seeds per second (**s/s**). The flow under which a line counts as failing. **“PLUS”** and **“MINUS”** change it by 1.
- **Control line** — the white line across the diagram: the alarm level drawn.
- **Measured flow** — the upper figure: the average of the lines now.
- **Green column** — the flow is above the alarm level.
- **Yellow column** — the flow is below the alarm level: alarm.
- **No column** — no flow at all. While the drill is seeding and the alarms are watched, the background of that column blinks dark red over its full height.

## “Hybrid” mode

As **“Flow”**, with three differences: the set value is a **target rate in seeds per metre** (**s/m**), changed by 1; lines for the permitted deviation can be drawn above and below it; and skips and doubles are not counted.

## “Precise” mode

![The seed diagram in the Precise mode with skips and doubles.](figures/diagram-precise)

- **Target rate** — the lower figure of the rate field, in seeds per metre (**s/m**), changed by 0.1. While you change it, the panel also shows it as a population in **ks/Ha** and as the spacing between seeds in centimetres.
- **Measured rate** — the upper figure, averaged over the lines that have flow now.
- **Rate line** and the **upper and lower deviation lines.** Which of them are drawn is set by **“Grid”**: the rate line with **“No”** or **“Full”**, the deviation lines with **“Partial”** or **“Full”** ([Seeding diagram settings](settings-menu.md)). The permitted deviation is **“Rate error,%”** of the seed sensors.
- **Green column** — within the deviation; **blue** — above it; **yellow** — below it.
- **Yellow hatched bar** left of a column — the skips in that line; **blue hatched bar** right of it — the doubles. Their height is measured against **“Scale S&D,%”**, shown at the top of the rate field while **“Skips & Doubles”** is **“Yes”**. On machines with many rows the columns are too narrow and the bars are not drawn.

Skips, doubles and the quality are counted over the **recalculation interval** — the stretch of path set by **“Recalculation,m”** of the seed sensors.

## Marks on a column — all modes

| **Mark** | **Meaning** |
| --- | --- |
| White box with **!** | The sensor is taken out of control. |
| Red cross | No connection to the sensor. |
| Grey background, white number | The sensor selected in the sensor setup mode. |
| Light grey hatching | The line is shut off for a tramline — see [Next tramline bout](next-tramline-bout.md). |

## “NOT UNDER CONTROL”

The panel starts watching the seeding alarms only when the drill is really seeding: when at least the share of lines set by **“Percent of sowing,%”** (20 % by default) sows within the set value — and, if **“Seeding criteria”** is set in the speed sensor, while the drill moves. Seed and fertilizer alarms start and stop together. **One short beep** says the watching has started; **three short beeps**, that it has stopped.

If the drill is seeding but the flow stays under the set value, the diagram shows **“NOT UNDER CONTROL”**. Either the flow has fallen during work — a real fault — or the alarm level or target rate is set higher than the machine delivers.

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **Columns under the line are not guarded.** Set the level so that the columns stand above the line, or let the panel set it: [Set the alarm level](set-the-alarm-level.md).


# GPS reception and the GPS information screen

The panel has a GPS receiver built in. It gives the travel speed where the drill has no wheel or radar sensor, or alongside one. While the receiver answers and has a valid fix, the speed comes from GPS. If it falls silent or loses the signal, the sensor set under **“Speed”** in the [profile](profile.md) takes over by itself — you do not have to switch anything.

The receiver is switched on by the profile item **GPS**: **UBX** for the built-in receiver (the normal setting) or **NMEA**; **“No”** switches it off and hides the satellite icon.

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **GPS needs a speed sensor in the profile.** Without one, the **GPS** item snaps back to **“No”** when the profile is saved. On a drill without a drive wheel it is enough to set **“Speed”** to **“Control panel”** without connecting a sensor there — this takes no place on the sensor network. Then, if the GPS signal is lost, the panel shows no travel speed until reception returns.

## The satellite icon

The icon stands at the right edge of the home screen, with the number of satellites used in its lower right corner.

![The satellite icon in its states: receiver silent, no fix, 3, 6 and 12 satellites.](figures/gps-satellite-icon)

| **Colour** | **Meaning** |
| --- | --- |
| Red | The receiver does not answer, or it answers without a valid fix — normal indoors and just after switch-on. The number is not shown while the receiver is silent. |
| Grey | Valid fix, fewer than 5 satellites. |
| Yellow | Valid fix, 5 to 7 satellites. |
| Grey | Valid fix, 8 satellites or more. The two grey states differ only by the number. |

## The information screen

To open it, hold **“MENU”** on the home screen, select the satellite icon with **“UP”** / **“DOWN”** and press **“MENU”**.

::: {.anatomy fig="gps-information-screen"}
1. **“GPS signal:”** **“Yes”** if the receiver answers, otherwise **“No”**.
2. **Satellites** — the number seen and the number used in the fix.
3. **Speed** — the speed as the seeding uses it. Below a small standstill threshold it shows 0 km/h, so that a drill standing still does not count area.
4. **raw** — the unfiltered speed, and whether the fix is valid.
5. **UTC** — date and time from the receiver; zeros before the first valid fix.
6. **Reception counters.** With **NMEA**: bytes received, valid sentences, checksum errors and the baud rate found; with **UBX**: bytes, frames and errors.
7. **ring drop** — bytes lost in the receive buffer. A rising figure means the connection to the receiver is disturbed.
8. **BACK** leaves the screen.

The GPS information screen, receiver set to NMEA, on the bench.
:::

The screen only shows; nothing on it can be changed, and no access code is needed.


# The Seeding table screen

The **Seeding table** answers what the diagram on the home screen cannot: *which line exactly, and by how much.* Open it with **“HOME”** from the home screen; the next **“HOME”** goes on to the Statistics screen, **“BACK”** returns to the home screen.

The figures belong to the **working session**: they count from switch-on and are lost at switch-off. The field statistics are kept apart — see [The Statistics screen](statistics-screen.md).

## What the table shows

::: {.anatomy fig="mini-table-rate-path"}
1. **Row number** — the seed line, in the order of the rows of the machine.
2. **sds/m** — the rate measured **now**, in seeds per metre. **-----** — the line is watched but not sowing.
3. **Q.%** — quality: the share of seeds placed singly, as intended.
4. **Db%** — doubles: two seeds where one was intended.
5. **Sk%** — skips: a gap where a seed was intended.
6. **Page indicator** — this table and the number of tables, between the signs of **“MINUS”** and **“PLUS”**, the buttons that change the table. Absent if there is only one table.
7. **Population** of the line, in thousands of seeds per hectare.
8. **Averages** over all lines watched. With two groups of sensors, two such lines, **A** and **B**.

The first table of a 12-row planter in the “Precise” mode, standing still.
:::

Columns 3 to 7 belong to the **last completed recalculation interval** — the stretch set by **“Recalculation,m”** (or **“Recalculation,sec”** without a speed sensor), shown at the bottom right. Only column 2 is a live reading. After the machine stops, the figures of the last interval stay on the screen to be read at leisure. A further column, **%**, gives the deviation of each line from the target, with its sign; positive means more seeds and a closer spacing.

## Which tables your machine has

| **Table** | **Shown when** |
| --- | --- |
| **Rate per area** (population, ks/Ha), **Rate per distance** (seeds per metre) | Seed in the **“Precise”** mode. |
| **Seed counters** | Always. |
| **Dry fertilizer** | There are fertilizer sensors and their mode is not **“Precise”**. |
| **Liquid fertilizer** | There are liquid fertilizer sensors. |

A planter with seed in **“Precise”** and dry-fertilizer sensors has four tables. **“PLUS”** goes to the next one, **“MINUS”** to the previous one; the page indicator at the top right shows which one you are on.

![Table 1 of 4 — rate per area: seeds per metre, quality, doubles, skips and the population of every line.](figures/mini-table-view-1)

![Table 2 of 4 — rate per distance: the same columns with seeds per metre in place of the population.](figures/mini-table-view-2)

![Table 3 of 4 — seed counters: seeds counted per line and the bar of the deviation.](figures/mini-table-view-3)

![Table 4 of 4 — dry fertilizer: the flow of every fertilizer line and its deviation.](figures/mini-table-view-4)

If seed and fertilizer are both in **“Precise”**, the fertilizer lines appear in the seed tables as group **B**, in light yellow type.

![The Seed counters table: seeds per line and a bar of the deviation from the target.](figures/mini-table-counters)

On the **Seed counters** table the bar runs between the permitted deviation **“Rate error,%”** either side of the target — not a fixed scale. In the **“Flow”** and **“Hybrid”** modes the scale is fixed at −50 % to +50 %. The left column then shows seeds per second instead of seeds per metre.

## Markers and colours

| **In the rate column** | **Meaning** |
| --- | --- |
| **-----** | Watched, not sowing now. |
| **! ---**, whole row grey | Taken out of control. |
| **X ---**, whole row dark red | No connection to this sensor. |
| **? ---**, whole row dark red | A sensor of the wrong type answers here. |

While sowing, a cell turns **yellow** when it reaches more than half the permitted deviation and **red** when it exceeds it. The limits are **“Rate error,%”**, **“Doubles error,%”** and **“Skips error,%”** of the seed sensors; with the doubles or skips check off, **“Scale S&D,%”** is used. The row number turns yellow or red with its worst cell, so the line that stands out is found at a glance.

> **TIP**
>
> **Read the deviation first.** A line 20 % below the others has a problem the average will not show — a partly blocked outlet, a worn disk, a sensor that needs cleaning.

## Buttons

| **Button** | **What it does** |
| --- | --- |
| **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”** | Next / previous table. |
| **“DOWN”** / **“UP”** | Scroll one row. One touch is one row. |
| **“MENU”** | Asks **“Zero readings?”** — [Zero the readings](zero-the-readings.md). |
| **“HOME”** | Statistics. |
| **“BACK”** | Home screen. |

The table itself does not react to touch.

## Fertilizer tables and tramline rows

![The Dry fertilizer table.](figures/mini-table-fert)

The **Dry fertilizer** table is built like the Seed counters table, with **fert/m** in the **“Hybrid”** mode or **fert/s** in **“Flow”**; the piece count is shown only with **“Count seeds always”** on. The **Liquid fertilizer** table shows per line the flow and the litres applied, with **L/Ha** or **L/min** by **“Mode of liq.fert.”**, and has no deviation bar.

A line shut off for a tramline shows only its number and flow; the other columns are dashed. Here yellow and red warn that **more** seed falls into the tramline than **“Toler.sowing to tramline,%”** allows.

![A tramline row among the other rows.](figures/mini-table-tramline)


# The Statistics screen

The Statistics screen is the report of the work: how far you drove, how much you covered, what was sown and how evenly. It is kept **separately for each field** and survives switching off. Open it with **“HOME”** from the Seeding table (twice from the home screen); **“BACK”** returns to the home screen, **“HOME”** goes on to the next working screen.

The report is one long list. **“UP”** and **“DOWN”** scroll it one line per touch; **“PLUS”** and **“MINUS”** show the next or previous field. On the screen itself, a swipe up or down scrolls, a two-finger swipe changes the field and a two-finger tap opens the menu.

## The head and the work on the field

::: {.anatomy fig="stat-screen"}
1. **Field number**, between the signs of **“MINUS”** and **“PLUS”**.
2. **(A)** — this is the active field, the one the panel writes to now.
3. **Path** — distance driven while seeding, in km.
4. **Area** — area treated while seeding, in ha.
5. **Operating time** — time spent seeding.
6. **Movement speed** — the average speed while seeding.
7. **Started / Ended** — when the work on this field began and ended.
8. **Seeding** — the area sown, not sown and unknown.
9. **Seed sensors** — one block per sensor follows.
10. **s, n, ?** — the share of sown, not sown and unknown area for this sensor.
11. **Bar** — the same shares in colour: green sown, red not sown, grey unknown.
12. **Scroll bar** — where you are in the report.

The report of field 1, the active one, in the short view.
:::

**Unknown** is area driven while a sensor had no connection or was out of control. In the **“Flow”** mode, **not sown** is the area where the sensor saw no flow; in **“Precise”** it is the area of one skip times the number of skips.

## Blocks you may also see

| **Block** | **What it holds** |
| --- | --- |
| Products by weight | Per product: the weight applied, actual against target in kg/ha and in per cent, and the distance, share and number of deviations beyond **“Product rate error,%”**. |
| **“Work without alarms control”** | Path, area and share, time and speed driven while seeding without the alarms watched — a set value too high, or set high on purpose. |
| **“Speed control”** | **“Path, slow”** and **“Path, fast”**: distance and share driven outside the speed limits. Only with the speed control on. |
| **“Fertilizing”** | Fertilized, not fertilized and unknown area. |
| Per seed sensor, in the full view | The distance, share and number of times the line ran under the alarm level. |

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **The weight is right only after a calibration.** Calibrate the dispenser again after changing the metering roller, adjusting the variator or gearbox, or changing the seed.

## In the “Precise” mode

![The Seeding block in the Precise mode.](figures/stat-precise)

The **“Seeding”** block adds **“Seeds sown (x1000)”**; **“Quality”** (singles), **“Doubles”** and **“Skips”** while seeding, and **“Not sown”** — skips over stretches where nothing was sown — each as a share of all seeds and skips; and **“Population,ks/Ha”** and **“Rate, s/m”**, each in the columns **“Factical”** and **“Setuped”**, with the ratio in per cent. Each seed sensor adds its seeds, its quality, doubles and skips, its population and rate, and the distances it ran below and above the permitted deviation. **“Seeds sown (x1000)”** also appears in the other modes with **“Count seeds always”** on.

The actual rate counts only the path where seed flowed; the population counts the whole path. Their deviations can therefore differ.

## The menu of the screen

Press **“MENU”**.

![The menu of the Statistics screen.](figures/stat-menu)

| **Item** | **What it does** |
| --- | --- |
| **“Select field”** | Makes the field shown the active one — see [Start a new field](start-a-new-field.md). Shown only on a field that is not active. |
| **“Statistics”** | **“Short”** or **“Full”** view. Not shown without a speed sensor. |
| **“Mileage”** | Path and area over the whole life of the system; they cannot be reset. Without a speed sensor, the running time. |
| **“Save to SD-card”** | Shown when a memory card is ready. Firmware 2.2.8 does not save the report yet and answers with a failure message. |
| **“Zero statistics”** | Erases the field shown. At the Operator level the panel asks for the code of a higher level; above it, **“Are you sure?”**. |

![The lifetime mileage of the system.](figures/stat-distance)


# The rate control screen

On the rate control screen you set the target rates of seed, dry fertilizer, liquid fertilizer and the products applied by weight, and watch the rate actually applied. It also shows the area, the speed, the hoppers, the fans and the implement position. It is the last working screen: **“HOME”** from the Statistics screen (or the Motors screen) brings you here, and one more **“HOME”** returns to the home screen. **“BACK”** does not leave this screen.

It is the only screen the panel remembers over switch-off: if it was open, it opens again after the next switch-on.

## What the screen shows

::: {.anatomy fig="mini-rate-screen"}
1. **Area** worked on the active field, in **ha**. Only with a speed sensor.
2. **Travel speed**, in km/h, with the same messages as on the home screen — see [Speed](indicators.md#speed). Only with a speed sensor.
3. **Settings symbol.** Touch and hold it to open the main menu.
4. **Product indicator** — here product 1, in kg/ha. One for every product that has at least one metering unit under control applying it by weight.
5. **Rate.** The rate actually applied; while the indicator is selected, the target.
6. **Work pause** — the hand. Dark grey: working; blinking yellow: application locked — see [Lock application by hand](lock-application-by-hand.md).
7. **Hopper**, one for every hopper.

The rate control screen of a drill with one product applied by weight, standing still.
:::

Depending on the machine, more indicators appear: the target rate of liquid fertilizer in L/ha, the rate of seed and of dry fertilizer in the **“Precise”** mode, a fan indicator for every fan, and the implement position at the bottom right. If there is no room for all fans and hoppers, the panel drops first a fan, then hoppers; the home screen still shows them all.

## Three states

- **Observation** — nothing is selected. The indicators show the rates actually applied.
- **Rate change** — **“PLUS”** or **“MINUS”**. The rate indicators can be selected; see [Change the target rate](set-the-target-rate.md).
- **Sensor setup** — hold **“MENU”**. The settings symbol, the speed, the fans, the hoppers and the implement position can be selected; **“PLUS”** and **“MINUS”** take the selected sensor into or out of control, **“MENU”** opens its context menu — or, on the settings symbol, the main menu.

In both modes **“UP”** and **“DOWN”** move the selection, **“BACK”** leaves the mode, and **“HOME”** held locks or unlocks application.

## Colours of a rate indicator

| **What you see** | **Meaning** |
| --- | --- |
| Symbol and unit green, value white | In order; the value is the rate applied. |
| Symbol, unit and value blinking red | The rate applied deviates from the target more than allowed. |
| Dark blue-green background, light blue symbol, yellow value | Selected; the value is the target. |
| **!!!!**, **XXXX** or **????** blinking red (liquid fertilizer only) | Not under control / no connection / a device of the wrong type. |

In the **“Precise”** mode the seed and fertilizer indicators show the population in **ks/Ha** while not selected, and the target in **s/m** while selected.

The rate of a product is averaged over each 10 m of travel. It counts as deviating when it is off by more than **“Product rate error,%”**: the alarm comes after two such stretches in a row and clears after two good stretches. Standing still, with application locked, or with no metering unit under control, the indicator shows 0.00 and the alarm is cleared.

## To the motors and their calibration

Touch and hold a product indicator — or select it in the rate change state and press **“MENU”**. A list of the motors of that product opens (**“Motor”** or **“Fert.mot.”** with the number). Select a motor and press **“MENU”**: **“Calibration, product”**, **“Weight, gr”** and **“Rotations”**. How to calibrate: [Calibrate a motor by weight](calibrate-motor-weight.md).

The list exists only for products whose motors work in **“Flow”** or **“Hybrid”**. If the machine is moving, the panel refuses: the speed must be zero for a calibration. A touch and hold on the liquid fertilizer indicator opens the context menu of the pump.


# The Motors screen

The Motors screen shows the dispenser electric motors of the machine, one tile each, and the tramline actuators. It is the screen to look at when a row stops sowing and you want to know whether the motor is the reason. It has no heading: it carries only numbered motor and actuator symbols — no rates, no area, no speed.

It exists if the profile holds at least one seed motor, one fertilizer motor or one tramline actuator, and it is shown **only above the Operator level** — enable the Agronomist level first ([Enable the Agronomist level](enable-agronomist-level.md)). Then it follows the Statistics screen: three presses of **“HOME”** from the home screen. **“HOME”** goes on to the rate control screen; **“BACK”** returns to the home screen.

![The Motors screen of a planter with eight seed motors.](figures/mini-motors-screen)

The **seed motors** stand in a bar at the top, numbered in the order of the profile. Below it a bar of **fertilizer motors**, if the machine has them — on a machine with more than twenty rows and no fertilizer motors, the second bar holds the second half of the seed motors. The **tramline actuators** stand below the bars. Beside each motor: the speed of the driven shaft in rpm; on machines with many motors it is left out so that all tiles fit.

## Reading a motor tile

The colour of the symbol is the state. Symbol and sign alternate once a second while the state is not normal.

| **Symbol** | **Value** | **State** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Motor, **green** | the speed | Under control and driven. |
| Motor and **STOP**, yellow | the speed | In order, but **application is off** — at the headland, or locked by hand. Not a fault. |
| Motor, **red** | the speed | Alarm. The alarm window names the reason. |
| Motor and cross, red | **XXX** | No connection to the motor controller. Check its power supply and its cable and connectors. |
| Motor and **?**, red | **???** | The device answering is not a motor controller, or the controller stayed in its update mode. |
| Motor struck through | **!!!** | Taken out of control: neither driven nor watched. |

![Three tiles: green in order, red with XXX, struck through.](figures/mini-motors-tile-states)

> **NOTE**
>
> **Yellow is not a fault.** A screen of yellow STOP signs means application is switched off. Red is a fault; yellow is a state you chose.

## Reading a tramline actuator

| **Symbol** | **State** |
| --- | --- |
| Pulled in or pulled out, **grey**, steady | It has reached that position. |
| Pulled in or pulled out, **yellow**, steady | It is moving there. |
| Pulled in and pulled out alternating, yellow | The position is not certain. |
| Red cross, blinking | No connection. |
| Red question mark, blinking | The device answering is not a tramline actuator. |
| Actuator symbol, red, blinking | The actuator reports an alarm. |
| Struck through, grey, blinking | Taken out of control. |

The position reached is grey, not green: only motors are green here.

## Selecting a motor

Hold **“MENU”** to switch on the selection; it stands on the first motor, on a white background. **“UP”** and **“DOWN”** move through a bar and on into the next bar and the actuators. Then:

- **“MENU”** opens the context menu of the selected motor or actuator — [Motor context menu](motor-context-menu.md).
- **“MINUS”** / **“PLUS”** take it out of or into control — [Take a sensor into or out of control](sensor-in-and-out-of-control.md).
- **“BACK”** leaves the selection; a second **“BACK”** returns to the home screen.

![The Motors screen with motor 3 selected.](figures/mini-motors-focus)

## The service screen of the motors

The context menu item **“Electric motors”** (Service level) opens a screen for the service engineer: versions, motor type, target and actual speed, error code, voltages, temperature, current and sixteen state signs in the **“Registers”** view, and counters per field in the **“Statistics”** view. You do not need it for sowing.

::: {.anatomy fig="mini-motors-service-statistics"}
1. **Mode** — **“HOME”** switches between the views.
2. **Motor number** — **“MINUS”** and **“PLUS”** switch the motor.
3. **Name of the view.**
4. **Field number** — **“UP”** and **“DOWN”** switch it; **(A)** marks the active field.
5. **Counters** — **“Jammed”**, **“Disconnects”** and **“Other”**. Above zero, red.
6. **In failure** — distance driven with the motor in failure.

The Statistics view of motor 1, field 1.
:::

**“BACK”** leaves the screen. If the number belongs to no motor of the profile, **“No data”** appears.


# Change the target rate or the alarm level

Every diagram and every product applied by weight has a **rate field**: the measured value on top, the set value below. What the set value is depends on the mode — see [The section diagram](section-diagram.md):

| **Mode** | **The set value** | **One step** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **“Flow”** | Alarm level, seeds per second | 1 s/s |
| **“Hybrid”** | Target rate, seeds per metre | 1 s/m |
| **“Precise”** | Target rate, seeds per metre | 0.1 s/m (0.5 to 50.0) |
| Product by weight | Target rate, kg/ha | 0.1 kg/ha up to 50.0, above that 1 kg/ha (1.0 to 999.0) |
| Liquid fertilizer | Target rate, L/ha | 0.1 L/ha up to 50.0, above that 1 L/ha |

## On the home screen

::: steps
1. Press **“PLUS”** or **“MINUS”** once. The rate field used last is selected and blinks; nothing has changed yet.

   ![Changing the target rate of a product in kg/ha on the home screen.](figures/rate-mass-change)

2. If the machine has more than one rate field — seed and fertilizer, products by weight — press **“DOWN”** or **“UP”** to move to the next or the previous one.

3. Press **“PLUS”** to raise the value or **“MINUS”** to lower it, one step per touch. Holding the button does not repeat it.

4. Press **“BACK”** to finish, or simply wait: five seconds after the last touch the field stops blinking. The new value is in force.
:::

In the **“Precise”** mode the panel also shows, while you change the target, the same rate as a population in **ks/Ha** and as the spacing between seeds in centimetres.

## On the rate control screen

::: steps
1. Press **“PLUS”** or **“MINUS”**. The target selected last is highlighted — dark blue-green background, yellow value; after switch-on, **“Product 1”**. The first press changes nothing.

   ![The rate control screen with Product 2 selected for a change.](figures/mini-rate-edit)

2. Move to the target you need with **“UP”** and **“DOWN”**.

3. Set the value with **“PLUS”** and **“MINUS”**.

4. Press **“BACK”**. The highlight goes; the indicators show the applied rates again.
:::

Coming down from above 50.0, a product or liquid rate stops exactly at 50.0; the next touch takes it below, in steps of 0.1. The seed target in the **“Precise”** mode is one number for all seed sensors: the home screen and the rate control screen change the same value, and there is no menu item for it.

The value is stored by itself about one and a half seconds after the last change; wait that long before switching off.

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **Columns under the line are not guarded.** Set far above what the machine delivers, the columns sink under the line and the panel shows **“NOT UNDER CONTROL”**. On a grain drill, let the panel find the level: [Set the alarm level](set-the-alarm-level.md).


# Set the alarm level of a grain drill

In the **“Flow”** mode the panel watches every line against an **alarm level** in seeds per second: a line whose flow drops below it is reported. Set too high, the columns sink under the line and the diagram shows **“NOT UNDER CONTROL”**; set too low, a partly blocked line goes unnoticed. The simplest way is to let the panel set it from the flow it sees.

## Let the panel set it

::: steps
1. Start seeding as usual, at working speed, and wait until the panel gives **one short beep** — it is now watching the seeding.

2. On the home screen, hold **“BACK”**. The panel gives one short beep.

3. Look at the rate fields. In the **“Flow”** mode each alarm level is now **half** the flow measured at that moment; in the **“Hybrid”** mode the target rate is set to the rate measured at that moment. The changed field is highlighted.
:::

This works for the seed diagram, the fertilizer diagram and liquid fertilizer in **“Flow”**, all at once, but only **while the panel watches the seeding**. Standing still, or in the **“Precise”** mode, the long press does nothing.

![The seed diagram with the alarm level in s/s and its control line.](figures/diagram-threshold)

## Set it by hand

Press **“PLUS”** or **“MINUS”** on the home screen: the first press selects the seed rate field, further presses change it by 1 s/s. **“DOWN”** and **“UP”** move to the fertilizer rate field. Details: [Change the target rate](set-the-target-rate.md).

> **TIP**
>
> **Check after the first pass.** Every column should stand clearly above its line. If several columns hover close to it, lower the level a little; if the diagram shows “NOT UNDER CONTROL” while the drill sows well, the level is too high.


# Lock product application by hand

On a machine with dispenser electric motors, fertilizer motors or a liquid fertilizer pump, you can lock product application by hand. While it is locked, no dispenser motor turns, the pump stands still, and the panel expects no application: alarms about a rate that is too low do not occur. Use it whenever you work on the metering units, or to cross a field without sowing.

> **WARNING**
>
> **The lock is a function of the panel, not a safety switch.** Before you put your hands into a metering unit, switch off the drive at the machine as its manual requires.

::: steps
1. On the home screen or on the rate control screen, hold **“HOME”** until the panel gives one short beep.

2. Check the lock. On the home screen a yellow motor symbol blinks in the column at the right; on the rate control screen the hand at the bottom left turns yellow.

   ![The work pause hand: dark grey while working, yellow while locked.](figures/mini-rate-pause)

3. To release the lock, hold **“HOME”** again. One short beep; the symbol stops blinking and application resumes.
:::

On every other machine the long press does nothing and the hand stays dark grey.

On the Motors screen a locked motor shows a yellow **STOP** — see [The Motors screen](motors-screen.md).
> **NOTE**
>
> **On a bench with speed imitation** and dispenser motors, the panel starts with application locked and the imitated speed stays at 0. Only releasing the lock with **“HOME”** starts the imitated travel.


# Take a sensor into or out of control

A sensor taken **out of control** is no longer watched: it raises no alarms, and its indicator shows the blinking not-controlled sign. Do it only to keep working with a faulty sensor until it is repaired — and take it back into control afterwards.

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **A sensor out of control is blind, not quiet.** Nothing about that line or device is watched any more. A motor out of control is not driven either: its row is not sown.

::: steps
1. On the home screen, hold **“MENU”** until one device is shown on a white background. The panel is now in the sensor setup mode.

   ![The home screen in the sensor setup mode, the speed indicator selected.](figures/sensor-mode-enter)

2. Select the sensor with **“UP”** and **“DOWN”**. In a diagram, the selected column gets a grey background and a white number.

3. Press **“MINUS”** to take it out of control, or **“PLUS”** to take it back into control.

4. The panel asks whether you are sure. Press **“MENU”** for **“Yes”**, or **“BACK”** for **“No”**; the green **“Yes”** and red **“No”** on the screen can also be touched.

   ![The question before the control of a sensor is switched off.](figures/confirm-window)

5. Press **“BACK”** to leave the sensor setup mode.
:::

The question comes only the **first** time while you stay in the sensor setup mode. After that, **“PLUS”** and **“MINUS”** act on every further sensor without asking, so a whole row of sensors can be switched quickly. After you leave the mode, the panel asks again.

The same works on the rate control screen (hold **“MENU”**) and, for motors and tramline actuators, on the [Motors screen](motors-screen.md). The control of the speed sensor cannot be switched off.

## When the statistics must be erased

If the active field already holds data and the change alters the set of products being applied — possible with motors in the **“Flow”** and **“Hybrid”** modes — the panel first asks to **erase the statistics of the active field**. **“Yes”** erases them for good; at the Operator level it also asks for the code of a higher access level. To keep the data, select a field that is empty first — see [Start a new field](start-a-new-field.md).

## What the context menu offers

In the sensor setup mode **“MENU”** opens the context menu of the selected device: its information screen and its parameters, depending on the access level. The parameters of every sensor are in [Sensor settings](sensor-settings.md).


# Zero the readings of the Seeding table

The figures of the [Seeding table](table-screen.md) — seed counters, quality, doubles, skips, rates, litres of liquid fertilizer — count from switch-on. Zero them when you start a new field or a new seed lot.

::: steps
1. On the home screen, press **“HOME”**. The Seeding table opens.

2. Press **“MENU”**. The panel asks **“Zero readings?”**.

   ![The question before the readings are zeroed.](figures/mini-table-zero-dialog)

3. Press **“PLUS”** for **“Yes”**, or touch **“Yes”**. **“MINUS”**, **“No”** or **“BACK”** cancels.
:::

On **“Yes”** the readings of **all** sensors are zeroed — seed, dry fertilizer and liquid fertilizer — whichever table you are looking at. **Only the readings of this screen**: the field statistics are not touched.

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **Zeroing cannot be undone.** Do it at the start of a field or a lot, not to tidy the screen.

## What else zeroes them

- Selecting another active field on the [Statistics screen](statistics-screen.md).
- Erasing the statistics of the active field.
- Switching the panel off — the readings belong to the working session.

The interval figures — quality, doubles, skips and the rates — are also renewed by the panel itself with every completed recalculation interval once the machine moves again. The seed counters stay.


# Start work on a new field

The panel keeps the statistics of several fields. It writes to one of them, the **active field**, marked **(A)** on the [Statistics screen](statistics-screen.md). Before the first pass on a new field, make an empty field the active one.

::: steps
1. On the home screen, press **“HOME”** twice. The Statistics screen opens with the active field.

2. Press **“PLUS”** or **“MINUS”** until the field you want is shown. Fields without **(A)** are not active.

3. Press **“MENU”**. The menu of the screen opens.

   ![The menu of the Statistics screen.](figures/stat-menu)

4. Select **“Select field”** and press **“MENU”**. The item is shown only for a field that is not active.

5. The panel asks **“Are you sure?”**. Press **“PLUS”** for **“Yes”**. The field is now active, marked **(A)**, and the readings of the Seeding table start from zero.
:::

If the field already holds data from other products than the machine applies now, the panel first asks to erase that field; at the Operator level it also wants the code of a higher access level.

## Erase a field that holds old data

::: steps
1. Show the field on the Statistics screen and press **“MENU”**.

2. Select **“Zero statistics”** and press **“MENU”**.

3. At the Operator level, type the code of the Agronomist level on the [number pad](number-pad.md). Above Operator, the panel asks **“Are you sure?”** — press **“PLUS”** for **“Yes”**.
:::

The statistics of that field are erased for good. The lifetime totals under **“Mileage”** are not affected.

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **The statistics can also be erased by other changes.** Taking a motor into or out of control, or changing the product type of a motor, can demand that the statistics of the active field be erased first. Switch to an empty field before such changes if you want to keep the data.


# Fill the disks with seeds

This applies only to planters with seed **dispenser electric motors** in the **“Precise”** mode. Without seed motors in the profile, or in another mode, the menu item is not shown.

When the disks are driven by electric motors, they stand empty until the motors run. Drive off with empty disks and the first metres of every row get nothing: each disk first has to pick up seeds and carry them round to the drop point. Filling turns the disks while the machine stands still, so that sowing starts from the first metre.

> **WARNING**
>
> **The disks turn while the machine stands still.** Before you start, make sure nobody is near the metering units, the dispenser shafts or the drive. Up to eight motors start at once, and each turns for up to about nineteen seconds. From the cab the metering units cannot be seen.

::: steps
1. Stop the machine. While it moves, the item is hidden.

2. On the home screen, press **“MENU”**. Select the first item, **“Fill the disks with seeds”**, and press **“MENU”**. It is open at every access level.

3. The panel asks for confirmation. Press **“PLUS”** or touch **“Yes”**. **“MINUS”**, **“No”**, **“BACK”** or a touch beside the window cancels.

   ![The question before the disks turn.](figures/mini-fill-confirm)

4. Watch the tiles. Each motor turns its disk at **4 rpm of the driven shaft** until the seed sensor of its row registers the first seed. While the operation runs, the bottom line tells you that **“BACK”** aborts it.

   ![The operation running: tile 1 is done and green, the others are still turning.](figures/mini-fill-running)

5. When every motor has finished, the panel gives **three short beeps** and shows **“Operation complete.”** Read the tiles at leisure, then press **“BACK”** to return to the main menu.
:::

To stop early, press **“BACK”**: every motor stops at once, goes back to the seeding logic, and the screen closes. You can start again straight away. On this screen only **“BACK”** works; the other buttons and touches do nothing.

## Reading the tiles

![The end of the operation: tile 1 green, tiles 2 to 4 failed.](figures/mini-fill-complete)

| **Tile** | **State** |
| --- | --- |
| Dark grey, full height | Waiting its turn — only eight motors run at once. |
| Yellow, upper part | Running: the disk is turning. |
| Green, upper part | Done: the seed sensor registered a seed. |
| Dark red, full height, bright red number | **Failed**: the disk could not be filled. The letters say why. |

A motor fails if no seed is registered within **1.25 turns of the shaft — about nineteen seconds**. A motor that reports a fault is stopped and failed at once; a motor out of control does not turn and counts as failed. Extra motors without a seed sensor of their own turn their disks but are reported as failed, because no seed can be seen. Fertilizer motors take part only if they too run in **“Precise”**, each paired with the fertilizer sensor of the same number.

## Letters on a failed tile

The letters stand always in the same places — **m** left, **g** middle, **s** right — and **red means a fault, white means out of control.**

![A failed tile close up.](figures/mini-fill-tile-failed)

| **Letter** | **Meaning** |
| --- | --- |
| **m** red | A fault of the motor during the operation. |
| **m** white | The motor is out of control and cannot run. |
| **g** red | The seed sensor saw no seed while the disk turned. |
| **s** red | A fault of the seed sensor during the operation. |
| **s** white | The seed sensor is out of control, or the motor has no seed sensor paired with it. |

If the seed sensor is out of control, a serviceable motor still turns the disk about one and a quarter turns, so the disk does get filled — but the panel reports a failure, because it never saw a seed.


# Assign a product to a dispenser motor

Every dispenser electric motor drives one dispenser and belongs to exactly one product. The panel keeps up to three products: **“Product 1”**, **“Product 2”** and **“Product 3”**. Several motors may apply the same product; its rate is then set once for all of them. In the factory state **all** motors are **“Product 1”**.

This needs the Agronomist level ([Enable the Agronomist level](enable-agronomist-level.md)) and motors in the **“Flow”** or **“Hybrid”** mode.

> **CAUTION**
>
> **The active field may have to be erased.** If the active field already holds data, the panel demands that its statistics be erased before the product type changes; **“Yes”** erases them for good. Select an empty field first if you want to keep them — [Start a new field](start-a-new-field.md).

::: steps
1. Go to the Motors screen and hold **“MENU”**. The first motor is selected.

   ![The Motors screen with a motor selected.](figures/mini-motors-focus)

2. Select the motor with **“UP”** and **“DOWN”**.

3. Press **“MENU”**. The context menu opens.

4. Go to **“Type of product”** with **“DOWN”**.

5. Choose the product with **“PLUS”** and **“MINUS”**.

   ![Type of product before and after the change.](figures/mini-motors-product-type)

6. If the panel asks to erase the statistics, press **“MENU”** for **“Yes”** or **“BACK”** for **“No”**.

   ![The question before the product type is changed on a field with data.](figures/mini-motors-product-change-confirm)

7. Press **“BACK”**. You are back on the Motors screen. Repeat from step 2 for every other motor.
:::

While you step through the values, a product that a dispenser shaft with weight control already applies is skipped — one product is applied either by motors or by such dispensers, not by both. If no other product is available, the value does not move; that is not a fault.

Then set the rate of each product: [Change the target rate](set-the-target-rate.md), and calibrate each motor: [Calibrate a motor by weight](calibrate-motor-weight.md).


# Calibrate a dispenser motor by weight

The calibration tells the panel how much product the dispenser delivers per turn of its shaft. Without it, the panel cannot turn the rate in kg/ha into a shaft speed. Calibrate every dispenser separately, and again whenever the product or the seed lot changes. It applies to motors in the **“Flow”** and **“Hybrid”** modes.

**You need:** scales, a container to put under the dispenser, and the product in the hopper.

> **WARNING**
>
> **The dispenser shaft turns while the machine stands still.** Before you start, make sure nobody is near the dispensers, the shafts or the drive. From the cab they cannot be seen.

::: steps
1. Stop the machine. While it moves, the calibration item is hidden.

2. Open the context menu of the motor — on the [Motors screen](motors-screen.md), or from its product on the [rate control screen](rate-control-screen.md). Select **“Dispenser calibration(weight)”** (from the rate control screen: **“Calibration, product”**) and press **“MENU”**.

3. The first screen shows the target rates of the products in use — the product of this motor between arrows — and under **“Product dosage speed limitation:”** the lowest and highest travel speed at which the rates can be applied. Press **“PLUS”**.

   ![The first calibration screen with the speed limits.](figures/mini-motors-cal-workinfo)

4. The screen lists what to do before calibrating: weigh the empty container and note the weight, fill the hopper, put the container under the dispenser, fill the rotor cells. Press **“MENU”** to fill the rotor cells.

   ![The list of actions before the calibration.](figures/mini-motors-cal-fillrotor)

5. The motor turns the shaft and the **“Rotations”** counter runs. After **two turns** the panel stops the motor and returns. **“BACK”** stops it earlier.

6. Press **“UP”**. The screen lists the steps of the calibration itself: empty the container, put it under the dispenser, calibrate, stop the motor, weigh. Empty the container and put it back.

7. Press **“MENU”**. The motor runs and the dispenser fills the container. Collect as much as possible — **at least 1 kg, at most 60 kg**.

8. Press **“BACK”** to stop the motor.

9. After more than one shaft turn, the bottom line offers **“MINUS”** to complete the calibration. Press **“MINUS”**.

   ![The calibration screen with the line for completing it.](figures/mini-motors-cal-prepare)

10. Weigh the full container. On the [number pad](number-pad.md), type the **difference between full and empty, in grams**, and press **“MENU”**. The panel stores **“Weight, gr”** and **“Rotations”** and returns to the first screen.

    ![The number pad asking for the weight in grams.](figures/mini-motors-cal-weight)

11. Press **“BACK”** to leave.
:::

To discard the calibration instead of step 9, press **“BACK”**: the panel asks **“Are you sure?”** and discards on **“PLUS”**; **“MINUS”** returns to the calibration.

> **CAUTION**
>
