> **Overwrite the 10000 completely, and never accept an empty field.** The pad opens at 10000 every time. Values below 1000 g or above 60000 g are silently set to the limit; an empty field writes unusable values without a word, and the dispenser will no longer apply the rate.

The context menu afterwards shows not your grams but an equivalent pair of numbers; only their ratio matters. It is stored by itself.

## Messages during the calibration

| **Message** | **Meaning and what to do** |
| --- | --- |
| **“FAILURE”** with a reason, e.g. **“No connection”** or **“No data from rotation sensor”** | The link was lost, the motor reported an alarm, or no shaft turns arrived for ten seconds. The motor is stopped, nothing is stored. **“BACK”** returns to the first screen; start again. |
| **“All electric motors not controlled.”** | No motor is under control. Take the motor into control with **“PLUS”** on the Motors screen. |
| The motor name in red with **“Not controlled”**, **“No connection”** or **“FAILURE”** | The calibration cannot start until that state is cleared. |
| **“Can not provide dosage!”**, limits in red | The rates contradict each other: no speed meets them all. Change a rate, or the shaft speed limits — each line names the product that sets it. |
| **“Run calibration on the console”** | A push-button on the motor controller is set up: the motor runs only while the button is held. |
| The speed must be zero (in English in every language) | The machine is moving. Stop it. |

![The failure screen of the calibration.](figures/mini-motors-cal-failure)


# Set up the tramline rhythm

A **tramline** is the lane the sprayer will drive in later. You make it while sowing: the panel shuts off seed lines or motors on certain **bouts** — passes across the field. It counts the passes and starts again at the first after the last. The number of bouts and the list of which device shuts off on which bout make the **rhythm**. Example: four bouts, actuator 1 shutting off on bout 4 — every fourth pass leaves a tramline.

| **Limit** | **Value** |
| --- | --- |
| Rhythms stored | **Three**, one active at a time. Keep the patterns of the machines you work with. |
| Bouts in a rhythm | **1 to 50**. |
| Tramline actuators | **Four** at most; the profile item **“Tramline actuators”** sets how many. |
| Cut-off bouts per device | **Four**. |

The panel knows nothing more: there is no setting for a starting side or for the width of the tramline. Which seed lines an actuator physically shuts off is set in **“Relation of sensors to actuators”** ([Settings menu](settings-menu.md)); without it the panel counts the bouts but shuts off nothing.

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **Set up the profile first, the tramline afterwards.** Saving a profile takes over its whole set of settings, all three rhythms included — a rhythm set up before is gone. And check the number of bouts against the sprayer, not the drill: a wrong rhythm looks perfect until the sprayer has nowhere to drive.

The item **“Tramline”** exists only if the machine has a tramline actuator, or as many seed motors as seed sensors, or as many fertilizer motors as fertilizer sensors. Setting up needs the Agronomist level ([Enable the Agronomist level](enable-agronomist-level.md)).

::: steps
1. Press **“MENU”**, then open **“Settings”** → **“Seeding machine parameters”** → **“Tramline”**. Set **“Tramline”** to **“Yes”** with **“PLUS”**.

   ![The Tramline submenu.](figures/mini-tramline-menu)

2. Select **“Tramline rhythm settings”** and press **“MENU”**. The rhythm editor opens.

3. Choose the rhythm number with **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”**, press **“MENU”** and choose **“Select”**. **(“Active”)** appears beside the number. Without this the rhythm is stored but not used.

4. Press **“DOWN”** to the number of bouts, press **“MENU”**, set **“Bouts”** with **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”** and confirm with **“MENU”**.

5. Press **“DOWN”** into the empty row of a section and press **“MENU”**. Set the device number and the **“Bout”** on which it shuts off; confirm with **“MENU”**.

6. For further cut-off bouts of the same device, press **“PLUS”** to the cell with the **“MENU”** sign at the end of its row and press **“MENU”** — up to four.

7. Press **“BACK”**, or hold **“HOME”**. The rhythm is saved.
:::

## The rhythm editor

![The rhythm editor with a new rhythm: one bout, nothing shut off yet.](figures/mini-tramline-rhythm-form)

Read it top down: **“Rhythm”** with its number between arrows and **(Active)** if it is in use; under it the number of bouts in a box; then up to three sections — **“Tramline actuators activation”**, **“Tramline motors activation”**, **“Tramline fert. motors activation”** (with both modes **“Precise”**: **“Tramline motors gr.A activation”** and **“Tramline motors gr.B activation”**). Each row names a device — **“Actuator”**, **“Motor”**, **“Fert.mot.”** — and the bouts on which it shuts off; a cell with the **“MENU”** sign adds a bout or a row. A selected cell is white on blue.

| **Button** | **What it does** |
| --- | --- |
| **“UP”** / **“DOWN”** | One row up or down, across the sections. |
| **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”** | On the rhythm number: next / previous rhythm. In a row: one cell right / left. On the number of bouts: nothing — open it with **“MENU”**. |
| **“MENU”** | Opens the dialog of the selected cell. |
| **“BACK”** | Saves and returns to the **“Tramline”** menu. |
| **“HOME”** held | Saves and returns to the home screen. A short press does nothing here. |

## The dialogs

- **Rhythm number:** **“Select”** makes it the one in use; **“Reset rhythm settings”** deletes its rows and sets its bouts to 1.
- **Number of bouts:** lowering it deletes entries for bouts that fall away; a row left with no bout disappears. If the current bout was above the new number, counting restarts at 1.
- **Row of a device:** the device number and **“Remove”**. Numbers already used in the section are skipped — read the value, do not count presses.
- **Bout of a row:** **“Bout”**, **“Remove bout”** and **“Remove all bouts”**. Bouts already in the row are skipped. If every bout is already entered, **“Unused bouts are not found!”** appears instead; any button closes it.

> **CAUTION**
>
> **The delete items sit right below the value.** One **“DOWN”** too many and a **“MENU”** delete the row you are working on. **“Reset rhythm settings”** also discards unsaved changes to the other two rhythms and an unsaved **“Select”**.

## What is stored where

The three rhythms, the number of bouts, the current bout, **“Tramline”** and **“Auto-switching”** belong to the settings of the panel and are stored by themselves shortly after the last touch. The profile holds only how many devices there are; on opening, the editor clears rows for which the profile has no device. With **“Tramline”** at **“No”**, all actuators and motors return to sowing.

Working in the field: [Next tramline bout](next-tramline-bout.md).


# Tramline in the field — bout indicator and next bout

As soon as **“Tramline”** is set to **“Yes”** ([Set up the tramline rhythm](tramline-rhythm.md)), the home screen shows the **tramline indicator**: a wheel-track symbol, and beside it the current bout on top and, smaller, the number of bouts of the rhythm below. With markers in the profile it stands right of the marker indicator.

![The home screen during a cut-off bout: the tramline indicator and hatched columns.](figures/mini-tramline-home)

| **Symbol** | **Meaning** |
| --- | --- |
| Grey | The panel moves to the next bout by itself. |
| Yellow | It does not: **“Auto-switching”** is off, or the machine gives it nothing to switch by. |
| Yellow, alternating with a cross | The machine could switch by itself, but **“Auto-switching”** is off. |

The columns of the lines shut off are **hatched light grey**; the flow inside is still shown, hatched: green while it stays below the limit, red above it — and then the panel reports **“Seeding to tramline”**. The limit is a share of the target rate, **“Toler.sowing to tramline,%”** of the seed sensor ([Sensor settings](sensor-settings.md)). Over a sensor that does not answer or is out of control the hatching blinks.

## Change the bout by hand

::: steps
1. On the home screen, press **“BACK”**. The bout menu opens. If a rate field is blinking, the first **“BACK”** only stops the blinking; in the sensor setup mode **“BACK”** leaves the mode instead.

   ![The bout menu.](figures/mini-tramline-bout-menu)

2. To set a bout, select **“Active bout”** and change it with **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”**, from 1 to the number of bouts. It is taken over when the menu closes.

3. To advance one bout, select **“Next bout”** and press **“MENU”**. The menu closes. This item is there only when the panel cannot switch by itself.

4. Where the panel can switch by itself, the menu offers **“Auto-switching”** instead: **“MENU”** toggles it between **“Yes”** and **“No”**, beeps and closes the menu.
:::

No higher access level is needed for this.

## When the panel switches by itself

It needs something that tells it a bout has ended:

| **Machine** | **What ends a bout** |
| --- | --- |
| With markers | A change of the marker position. At least one marker sensor must be under control and answering. |
| Without markers | Lifting the drill out of work. The implement position sensor must be under control and answering. |
| Neither | Nothing — the menu offers **“Next bout”** in place of **“Auto-switching”**. |

Besides, **“Auto-switching”** must be **“Yes”** and the bout must really have been driven: while the machine moves (without a speed sensor: while it sows), switching is blocked. It is released when the work stops; the next marker change — or lift — then advances exactly one bout.

> **NOTE**
>
> **If the bout does not advance at the headland,** check in this order: is **“Auto-switching”** **“Yes”**; is the marker or the implement position sensor under control; does it answer. The first is a setting, the other two are the machine.

## The actuator itself

Two settings of a tramline actuator are in its context menu ([Sensor settings](sensor-settings.md)), Agronomist level:

| **Item** | **Values** |
| --- | --- |
| **“Cutoff position”** | The position in which it shuts off: **“Pulled out”** (factory setting) or **“Pulled in”**. |
| **“Switch”** | When it moves: **“when seeding”** (factory setting) or **“always”**. |

Two alarms concern the actuator: **“Illegal state”** — it reports both end positions at once; **“Stall”** — it does not reach the position asked. See [Tramline alarms](alarms-tramline.md).


# Access levels

The panel hides every setting a driver does not need. What a menu shows depends on the **access level** chosen under **“User”** in the **“Settings”** menu. After every power-on the panel starts at **“Operator”**.

| **Level** | **Who** | **What it opens** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **“Operator”** | The driver | Everything for work: the target rates, the fields, the statistics, **“Alarm delay”**, the date and time, the language. In the context menus: **“Information”** and the everyday sensor settings such as **“Fraction”** or **“Minimum, rpm”**. |
| **“Agronomist”** | The farmer, the dealer | Also **“Seeding machine parameters”** (working width, modes, calibrations), the hidden parameters of every sensor, and in the main menu the **“Service”** menu with **“Sensors Configuration”** for seed and pressure sensors. |
| **“Service”** | The service engineer | Also the profile, the configuration of HUB-8 concentrators and tramline actuators, the service screen of the motors, **“Reset to defaults”** in every context menu and **“Reset settings”**. The status screen of a sensor shows its address. |

The list under **“User”** has a fourth value, **“Debug”**. It is for the manufacturer and has no use in the field.

A raise to **“Agronomist”** or **“Service”** asks for the PIN of that level. The PINs are different for every panel: the dealer gives them for your panel. Going down asks nothing. How: [Enable the Agronomist level](enable-agronomist-level.md).

In this manual a parameter or menu item says which level it needs. An item you do not see is above your level, or does not apply to the machine in the profile.

## What happens to the alarms while the level is high

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **At “Agronomist” and “Service” the panel shows no alarm windows.** A fault on a sensor raises no window and no alarm signal until the level is back at **“Operator”**.

The only window that still comes is **“User is Agronomist! Alarms will not be shown!”** — once per session, as soon as the panel sees seeding at the higher level. See [User is Agronomist](alarms-access-level.md).

When you go back down to **“Operator”**, the panel drops the alarms that have cleared in the meantime and shows the ones that are still true, one after another.

## Back to Operator

- In **“Settings”** set **“User”** to **“Operator”** with **“MINUS”** and press **“MENU”**, or
- switch the panel off and on.

Do one of the two after every commissioning or repair, before the machine goes back to work.

## What is in the Service menu

The main menu shows **“Service”** from the **“Agronomist”** level on. What it holds:

| **Item** | **Level** | **What it is for** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **“Profile”** | Service | The list of devices of the machine. [The profile](profile.md) |
| **“Sensors Configuration”** | Agronomist | Gives a new or replaced device its address. [Device configuration](device-configuration.md) |
| **“Electric motors”** | Service | The service screen of the dispenser motors; only with motors in the profile. |
| **“Count seeds always”** | Agronomist | **“Yes”**: the Seeding table and the Statistics screen count seeds also in the **“Flow”** and **“Hybrid”** modes, not only in **“Precise”**. |
| **“Enter key”** | Agronomist | Shown only on a panel with a time-limited licence: enter the licence key from the dealer. |

The remaining items of this menu are for the service engineer and the manufacturer.


# Enable the Agronomist level

Sensor parameters, the working width, the calibrations and the device configuration need the **“Agronomist”** level. The **“Service”** level is raised the same way. What each level opens: [Access levels](access-levels.md).

You need the PIN of this panel for that level. It is different for every panel; the dealer gives it.

::: steps
1. On the home screen press **“MENU”**. The main menu opens.

   ![The main menu.](figures/menu-main)

2. Select **“Settings”** with **“UP”** / **“DOWN”** and press **“MENU”**. The **“Settings”** menu opens.

3. Press **“DOWN”** until **“User”** is selected — it is the last item. Press **“PLUS”** until it reads **“Agronomist”** (or **“Service”**).

   ![“User” set to Agronomist.](figures/menu-settings-user)

4. Press **“MENU”**. The PIN pad opens with **“Enter your PIN:”**; the line under the prompt identifies this panel. Type the PIN on the [number pad](number-pad.md) and touch **“OK”** or press **“MENU”**.

   ![The PIN pad.](figures/user-agronom-pin)

5. The panel shows the name of the new level for a moment and returns to the **“Settings”** menu, now with the items of that level — for example **“Seeding machine parameters”**.

   ![The panel confirms the new level.](figures/user-agronom-done)

6. Press **“BACK”** to leave the menu.
:::

If the PIN is wrong — or is the PIN of another level than the one chosen in step 3 — the panel shows **“Invalid PIN”** for a moment and opens the PIN pad again. Type it again, or press **“BACK”** to give up; the level stays as it was.

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **At “Agronomist” and “Service” no alarm windows are shown.** When you have finished, go back to **“Operator”**: repeat steps 1–3, choose **“Operator”** with **“MINUS”** and press **“MENU”** — no PIN is asked going down. Switching the panel off and on does the same.

When you come back down, the alarms that are still true are shown one after another — see [Access levels](access-levels.md#what-happens-to-the-alarms-while-the-level-is-high).


# Check the profile and the connections

The panel watches only the devices its **profile** lists. Systems are usually delivered with the profile already set, but before you set any parameter, check that it matches the machine and that every device answers. Checking the profile needs the **“Service”** level, which asks for a PIN — the dealer gives it for your panel; see [Enable the Agronomist level](enable-agronomist-level.md). The other two checks need no code.

## 1. Check the profile

::: steps
1. Connect all devices to the panel and power them as the wiring diagram in the data sheet of the system shows.

2. Switch the panel on. After the splash screen the home screen appears.

3. Raise the access level to **“Service”**: **“MENU”** → **“Settings”** → **“User”** → **“Service”**, **“MENU”**, PIN — as in [Enable the Agronomist level](enable-agronomist-level.md).

4. Press **“BACK”**. The main menu returns, now with **“Service”**. Select **“Service”** and press **“MENU”**, then select **“Profile”** and press **“MENU”**. The profile menu opens.

   ![The way to the profile: Settings with the Service level, the main menu, the Service menu, the profile menu.](figures/menu-to-profile)

5. Read the profile menu, from the top. Each item is one kind of device with the number the panel expects, for example **“Seed sensors”**; **“Speed”** shows how the speed sensor is connected: **“Control panel”**, **“Input device”** or **“Input device (2)”**. **“UP”** and **“DOWN”** go through the list, which is longer than the screen. All items: [The profile](profile.md).

   ![The profile menu.](figures/menu-profile)

6. Compare the list with the machine and the wiring diagram. Change nothing here: **“BACK”** leaves the profile menu without saving.

7. Go back to the **“Operator”** level: switch the panel off and on, as in [Enable the Agronomist level](enable-agronomist-level.md). At the **“Service”** level the panel shows no alarm windows, and the next check needs them.
:::

If the profile does not match the machine, set it up first: [Set up the profile](set-up-the-profile.md).

## 2. Check that every device answers

Wait a few seconds on the home screen. If no window **“Connection lost”** appears, the panel has found every device of the profile.

![“Connection lost” for fan sensor 1.](figures/alarm-link-lost-fan)

When several devices of one kind do not answer, one window lists all their numbers — here pressure sensors 1 to 3:

![“Connection lost” for three pressure sensors.](figures/alarm-link-lost-pressure)

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **A device that does not answer is not watched.** Check its connection against the wiring diagram and the profile once more. If you cannot find the cause, call the service — see [Device does not answer](alarms-any-device.md).

## 3. Check that every sensor is under control

A sensor **out of control** is not watched at all. Its indicator shows the blinking grey not-controlled sign, or **!!!!** in place of the value; under a diagram column it shows a white box with **!** — see [Indicators](indicators.md).

![The hopper sensor, the fan sensor and seed sensor 11 out of control.](figures/home-unmonitored)

If there is such a sensor, take it into control:

::: steps
1. On the home screen hold **“MENU”** until the speed indicator has a white background. The panel is in the sensor setup mode. Release the button.

   ![The sensor setup mode, the speed sensor selected.](figures/sensor-mode-enter)

2. Press **“DOWN”** (or **“UP”**) until the sensor out of control is selected. A seed sensor is selected when its number under the column has a white background.

   ![The fan sensor selected.](figures/sensor-selected)

3. Press **“PLUS”**. The panel asks whether you are sure; press **“MENU”** for **“Yes”**. **“BACK”** answers **“No”**.

   ![The question before the control of a sensor changes.](figures/confirm-window)

4. Repeat steps 2 and 3 for every sensor out of control. The question comes only the first time while you stay in this mode.

5. Press **“BACK”** to leave the sensor setup mode.
:::

Switching the control of a sensor on is what this manual calls *taking a sensor into control*. More: [Take a sensor into or out of control](sensor-in-and-out-of-control.md).

## The result

Every sensor must be under control, and no indicator may show a red cross — the sign of a device that does not answer.

When everything is right, the home screen shows every device in its normal grey, with no red cross and no not-controlled sign:

![All devices answer and are under control.](figures/home-all-ok)

Then go on with the settings: [Commissioning](commissioning.md).


# The profile

The **profile** tells the panel which devices the machine has and how many of each. It decides which indicators the home screen shows, which context menus exist and which devices the panel polls. A system is usually delivered with its profile set; change it only when the equipment of the machine changes. How to check it: [Check the profile and the connections](check-profile-and-connections.md). How to change it: [Set up the profile](set-up-the-profile.md).

The profile counts **what is watched and what is driven**, not boxes. One input device can carry, for example, fan sensors and hopper sensors together; one actuator controller can carry an actuator and two marker sensors. Each of them is entered under its own item.

::: {.anatomy fig="menu-profile"}
1. **“Seed sensors”** — the selected item.
2. **The value**, here 12, between **−** and **+**: change it with **“MINUS”** and **“PLUS”**.
3. **“Fertilizer sensors”**.
4. **“Liq.fert.flow sensors”**.
5. **“Hoppers”**.
6. **“Dispensers”**.
7. **“Speed”** — how the speed sensor is connected.
8. **Its value**, here **“Control panel”**.
9. **Scroll bar.** The list goes on below the screen.

The first items of the profile menu.
:::

## The items

Every item needs the **“Service”** level, like the menu itself.

| **Item** | **What it states** | **Values** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **“Seed sensors”** | Number of seed sensors. | 2 … 60 |
| **“Fertilizer sensors”** | Number of dry fertilizer sensors. | 0 … 60 |
| **“Liq.fert.flow sensors”** | Number of liquid fertilizer flow sensors. | 0 … 60 |
| **“Hoppers”** | Number of hopper level sensors. | 0 … 9 |
| **“Dispensers”** | Number of dispenser shaft sensors. | 0 … 9 |
| **“Speed”** | Whether there is a travel speed sensor and where it is connected: **“No”**; **“Control panel”** — one sensor on the panel; **“Input device”** — one sensor on an input device; **“Input device (2)”** — two sensors on an input device. | see left |
| **“GPS”** | The built-in GPS receiver as a speed source: **“No”**; **“UBX”** — the normal setting; **“NMEA”** — the receiver delivers its data in the NMEA 0183 format. While it has a valid fix, GPS takes priority over the sensor under **“Speed”**; without a fix the sensor takes over by itself. [GPS reception](gps-receiver.md) | see left |
| **“Fans”** | Number of fan speed sensors. | 0 … 2 |
| **“Pressure sensors”** | Number of pressure (vacuum) sensors. | 0 … 3 |
| **“Work position sensor”** | Whether there is a sensor for the working and transport position of the implement. | **“No”** / **“Yes”** |
| **“Markers”** | How the marker arms are watched: **“No”**; **“One”** — one sensor; **“Both”** — one sensor per arm. | see left |
| **“No battery charge”** | Battery charge sensor of the fan-drive engine. Switch it off together with the ignition sensor. | **“No”** / **“Yes”** |
| **“Emergency oil pressure”** | Low oil pressure sensor of the fan-drive engine. Switch it off together with the ignition sensor. | **“No”** / **“Yes”** |
| **“Ignition”** | Ignition key sensor of the fan-drive engine. | **“No”** / **“Yes”** |
| **“Low fuel”** | Fuel level sensor of the fan-drive engine. | **“No”** / **“Yes”** |
| **“Air filter”** | Air filter sensor of the fan-drive engine. | **“No”** / **“Yes”** |
| **“EMD of the seeds”** | Number of electric dispenser motors for seed. | 0 … 60 |
| **“EMD of the fertilizers”** | Number of electric dispenser motors for fertilizer. | 0 … 30 |
| **“Tramline actuators”** | Number of tramline actuators. | 0 … 4 |
| **“Liq.fert.pump controller”** | Whether there is a pump controller for liquid fertilizer. | 0 / 1 |
| **“Save profile”** | Saves the profile and restarts the panel. | — |

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **“GPS” works only with a speed sensor entered under “Speed”.** If **“Speed”** is **“No”**, the panel sets **“GPS”** back to **“No”** by itself. On a drill without a drive wheel set **“Speed”** to **“Control panel”** — no sensor needs to be connected there.

## Rules the profile must keep

**“Save profile”** refuses a profile that breaks one of these rules and shows **“Invalid profile!”**:

- at least **2 seed sensors**;
- **“Hoppers”**, **“Dispensers”** and the five engine sensors together: **at most 12**; above 10, **“Fans”** and **“Pressure sensors”** together may be at most 4;
- **“Fans”** and **“Pressure sensors”** together: **at most 5**;
- seed and fertilizer motors together: at most 60; fertilizer motors only together with seed motors and with fertilizer sensors;
- dispenser motors and a liquid pump controller need a speed sensor.


# Set up the profile

Set up the profile when the equipment of the machine changes — a device added, removed or of another kind. The items and their limits: [The profile](profile.md). The profile menu needs the **“Service”** level.

> **WARNING**
>
> **Change the profile only at commissioning, by the service.** A wrong profile makes the panel watch devices that are not there and ignore the ones that are.

::: steps
1. Connect all devices to the panel and power them as the wiring diagram in the data sheet of the system shows.

2. Switch the panel on. After the splash screen the home screen appears; what it shows depends on the present profile.

   ![The home screen after start-up.](figures/home-idle)

3. Raise the access level to **“Service”**: **“MENU”** → **“Settings”** → **“User”** → **“Service”**, **“MENU”**, PIN — as in [Enable the Agronomist level](enable-agronomist-level.md).

4. Press **“BACK”**. The main menu returns, now with **“Service”**.

5. Select **“Service”** and press **“MENU”**. The **“Service”** menu opens with **“Profile”** as its first item.

6. Select **“Profile”** and press **“MENU”**. The profile menu opens.

   ![The way to the profile: Settings with the Service level, the main menu, the Service menu, the profile menu.](figures/menu-to-profile)

7. Go through the items with **“UP”** / **“DOWN”** and set each with **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”** to the equipment of the machine.

   ![The profile menu.](figures/menu-profile)

8. Select **“Save profile”**, the last item, and press **“MENU”**. The panel asks **“Are you sure?”** — press **“PLUS”** for **“Yes”**, **“MINUS”** for **“No”**.

9. The panel asks you to wait, then shows **“Saved”** and **“Restart system”**, and restarts by itself. The new profile is in force after the restart.

   ![Saving the profile: the item Save profile, the question, then the message Saved and Restart system.](figures/profile-save)
:::

**“BACK”** leaves the profile menu; the device numbers you changed are not saved. **“GPS”** is the exception: it is stored at once, like a setting of the **“Settings”** menu.

## When the profile is not saved

| **The panel shows** | **Meaning** |
| --- | --- |
| **“No changes”** | The profile is the same as the stored one. Nothing is saved, nothing restarts. |
| **“Invalid profile!”** | The profile breaks a rule — too few seed sensors, too many small indicators, too many fans and pressure sensors, or motors without a speed sensor. See [Rules the profile must keep](profile.md#rules-the-profile-must-keep). Correct it and save again. |

After the restart the panel is at the **“Operator”** level. Check the result as in [Check the profile and the connections](check-profile-and-connections.md), then, if the machine makes tramlines, set up the tramline rhythm — always after the profile — [Set up the tramline rhythm](tramline-rhythm.md).


# The Settings menu

**“MENU”** on the home screen → **“Settings”**. The menu holds the general settings of the panel. Which items you see depends on the access level ([Access levels](access-levels.md)) and on the machine in the profile.

::: {.anatomy fig="menu-settings"}
1. **“Volume”** — the selected item.
2. **Its value between − and +.** **“PLUS”** and **“MINUS”** change it on the spot.
3. **“Language”**.
4. **“Buttons sound”**.
5. **“Change Date&Time”** — the arrow head opens a submenu.
6. **“Alarm delay”**, in seconds.
7. **“Seeding machine parameters”** — a submenu, from the Agronomist level.
8. **Scroll bar.** **“User”** follows further down.

The **“Settings”** menu at the Agronomist level.
:::

The panel stores every change by itself about one and a half seconds after the last change and the last touch of a button.

## The items

| **Item** | **Level** | **What it does** | **Range · default** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **“Volume”** | Operator | Loudness of the alarm signal, in per cent. | 0 … 100, steps of 10 · 100 |
| **“Language”** | Operator | Language of the texts on the screen: English, Ukrainian, Polish, Hungarian, Romanian, Bulgarian or German. | · English |
| **“Buttons sound”** | Operator | A short beep at every touch the panel accepts. | **“No”** / **“Yes”** · **“Yes”** |
| **“Seeding diagram settings”** | Operator | How the seed diagram of the home screen is drawn — [below](#diagram-settings). Shown only with a speed sensor and **“Mode of seeding”** at **“Hybrid”** or **“Precise”**. | submenu |
| **“Fertil. diagram settings”** | Operator | The same for the fertilizer diagram. Shown only with a speed sensor, fertilizer sensors and **“Mode of fertilizers”** at **“Hybrid”** or **“Precise”**. | submenu |
| **“Liq.fert. diagram settings”** | Operator | **“Grid”** of the liquid fertilizer diagram. Shown only with a speed sensor, liquid fertilizer sensors and **“Mode of liq.fert.”** at **“By area”**. | submenu |
| **“Change Date&Time”** | Operator | Date and time of the panel — [Set the date and time](set-date-and-time.md). | submenu |
| **“Alarm delay”** | Operator | How long a fault must last before the alarm window opens — [How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md). | 2 … 20 s · 3 s |
| **“Product rate error,%”** | Agronomist | Permitted deviation of the applied product weight from its target; beyond it the panel raises **“Rate of Product 1 is to low!”** or **“Rate of Product 1 is to high!”** (with the number of the product). Shown only when a product is dosed by weight, or with a liquid pump controller. | 3 … 20 % · 5 % |
| **“Seeding machine parameters”** | Agronomist | Working width, control modes, calibrations — [Seeding machine parameters](seeding-machine-parameters.md). | submenu |
| **“User”** | Operator | The access level — [Enable the Agronomist level](enable-agronomist-level.md). | **“Operator”** … **“Debug”** |
| **“Reset settings”** | Service | Returns the values of this menu and of **“Seeding machine parameters”** to the factory values at once, without asking — including **“Language”** (English), **“Width, cm”**, the modes, the active field and the **“GPS”** setting of the profile. | — |

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **The weight is calculated correctly only after a fresh dispenser calibration** whenever the metering roller has been changed, the variator or gearbox of the dispenser drive has been adjusted, or another seed is in the hopper. See [Calibrate the dispenser by weight](calibrate-dispenser-weight.md).

## Diagram settings

The submenus **“Seeding diagram settings”** and **“Fertil. diagram settings”** hold the same items, each for its own diagram. When the fertilizer sensors run in **“Precise”**, they are treated as a second seed group, and the items are named **“Seeding gr.A diagram”** and **“Seeding gr.B diagram”**.

| **Item** | **Level** | **What it does** | **Values · default** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **“Skips & Doubles”** | Operator | Shows or hides the columns of skips and doubles over the last completed stretch. Only in **“Precise”**. | **“No”** / **“Yes”** · **“Yes”** |
| **“Grid”** | Operator | **“No”** — only the target rate line; **“Partial”** — only the limits of the permitted deviation; **“Full”** — both. | · **“Full”** |
| **“Scale S&D,%”** | Operator | Full height of a skips or doubles column, in per cent of the diagram height. Only in **“Precise”**. | 5 … 50 %, steps of 5 · 20 % |
| **“Reset to defaults”** | Service | Returns the three items above to their defaults. | — |

What the diagram shows: [The section diagram](section-diagram.md).


# Set the date and time

The panel stamps the start and end of the work on every field with its clock, and shows the time on the home screen. **“Change Date&Time”** is in the **“Settings”** menu at the **“Operator”** level. What it opens depends on the **“GPS”** item of the [profile](profile.md).

## With GPS in the profile

::: {.anatomy fig="menu-datetime"}
1. **“Automatic”** — whether the clock follows the GPS receiver.
2. **Its value**, here **“No”**. Change it with **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”**.
3. **“Enter date and time”** — opens the menu for setting the clock by hand. Shown while **“Automatic”** is **“No”**.

The date and time menu of a panel with the built-in GPS receiver switched on.
:::

- **“Automatic”** at **“Yes”**: the clock takes the time from the GPS receiver. The item **“Time zone”** appears instead of **“Enter date and time”** — set your offset from UTC with **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”**, from −12:00 to +14:00 in whole hours.
- **“Automatic”** at **“No”**: select **“Enter date and time”** and press **“MENU”**, then go on as below from step 2.

## By hand

::: steps
1. **“MENU”** → **“Settings”** → **“Change Date&Time”**, press **“MENU”**. Without GPS in the profile the menu opens with **“Year”**, **“Month”**, **“Day”**, **“Hours”**, **“Minutes”**, **“Seconds”** and **“Set”**.

2. Select an item with **“UP”** / **“DOWN”** and change it with **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”**. **“MENU”** on a number — all items but **“Month”** — opens the [number pad](number-pad.md).

3. Set all six items. After a change of the month, a day that the month does not have is pulled back to its last day.

4. Select **“Set”** and press **“MENU”**. The clock takes the new date and time, and the menu you came from returns.
:::

**“BACK”** leaves without changing the clock. Every item opens with the present date and time, so you only change what is wrong.


# Seeding machine parameters

**“Settings”** → **“Seeding machine parameters”**, **“Agronomist”** level ([Enable the Agronomist level](enable-agronomist-level.md)). Set these first on a new machine — every figure of area and rate is worked out from them.

::: {.anatomy fig="menu-machine-params"}
1. **“Width, cm”** — the selected item.
2. **Its value between -[ and ]+**: **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”** step it, **“MENU”** opens the number pad.
3. **“Mode of seeding”**.
4. **Its value**, here **“Flow”**.
5. **“Speed calibration”** — starts the calibration of the speed sensor.

A machine with seed sensors only, a speed sensor and no dispenser sensors.
:::

| **Item** | **What it does** | **Range · default** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **“Width, cm”** | The working width of the machine. The area, and every rate per hectare, is worked out from it. **Always enter it.** | 100 … 2500 cm · 560 |
| **“Mode of seeding”** | How the seed sensors are controlled and shown: **“Flow”** — seeds per second, for grain drills; **“Hybrid”** — seeds per metre, possible on grain drills but not used in practice; **“Precise”** — seeds per metre with skips and doubles, for precision planters. | · **“Flow”** |
| **“Mode of fertilizers”** | The same three modes for the fertilizer sensors. Shown only with fertilizer sensors in the profile. | · **“Flow”** |
| **“Mode of liq.fert.”** | **“Flow”** or **“By area”** for the liquid fertilizer sensors. Shown only with such sensors and no pump controller. | · **“By area”** |
| **“Tramline”** | The tramline settings — [Set up the tramline rhythm](tramline-rhythm.md). Shown only if the machine can make tramlines. | submenu |
| **“Relation of sensors to actuators”** | Which seed lines each tramline actuator or motor shuts off. Shown only when that is not one to one. | screen |
| **“Speed calibration”** | [Calibrate the speed sensor](calibrate-speed.md). | — |
| **“Dispenser calibration”** | [Calibrate the dispenser rotation](calibrate-dispenser-rotation.md) for **“ALL”** dispensers or for one, by its number. Shown only with dispenser sensors in the profile. | **“ALL”**, 1 … number of dispensers |
| **“Reset to defaults”** | **“Service”** level. Returns the width and the modes to their defaults. | — |

Without a speed sensor in the profile the three mode items and **“Speed calibration”** are hidden: the panel can only work in **“Flow”**.

The target rate is set on the home screen, not here — [Change the target rate](set-the-target-rate.md). Its range follows the mode: **“Flow”** 1 to 1500 seeds per second, **“Hybrid”** 1 to 200 seeds per metre, **“Precise”** 0.5 to 50.0 seeds per metre.

## What a change does to the statistics

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **A new width or a change of mode to or from “Precise” erases the statistics of every field.** If any field holds data, the panel asks first — for the width **“Need to erase statistics!”** with **“PLUS”** for **“Yes”**, for the mode a message that the statistics must be erased, with **“MENU”** to delete and **“BACK”** to cancel. **“No”** or **“BACK”** keeps the old value. Note the figures you need before you change.

A change between **“Flow”** and **“Hybrid”** keeps the statistics.

The two modes depend on each other: the fertilizer sensors can run in **“Precise”** only while the seed sensors do. The panel refuses the other combinations with a message that names the item to change first. When both run in **“Precise”**, the fertilizer sensors become a second seed group, and the items read **“Mode of seeding gr.A”** and **“Mode of seeding gr.B”**.

If a product dosed by weight is then claimed both by a dispenser sensor and by a motor, the panel switches **“Weight control”** of the dispenser sensors off and says so in a **“WARNING!”** window.


# Sensor settings

Every sensor, motor and actuator has its own **context menu**: its status screen, its parameters and, for some, a calibration. The parameters of each kind of sensor are in the topics that follow this one.

## Reach a sensor

::: steps
1. On the home screen **hold “MENU”** until the speed indicator has a white background. The panel is in the sensor setup mode. Release the button.

   ![The sensor setup mode, the speed sensor selected.](figures/sensor-mode-enter)

2. Select the sensor with **“UP”** / **“DOWN”**. A selected seed or fertilizer sensor shows its number under the column on a white background.

3. Press **“MENU”**. The context menu of the selected sensor opens.

4. Change a value with **“UP”** / **“DOWN”** and **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”**, as in any menu. **“BACK”** closes the context menu; **“BACK”** once more leaves the sensor setup mode.
:::

What the context menu holds depends on the kind of sensor, on the machine and on the access level. A parameter you do not see is either above your level or does not apply — the topic of each sensor says which.

## The context menu

::: {.anatomy fig="ctx-speed"}
1. **“Information”** — opens the status screen of this sensor. Every context menu starts with it. [The sensor status screen](sensor-status-screen.md)
2. **An action of this kind of sensor** — here **“Speed calibration”**. A dispenser sensor has **“Dispenser calibration(weight)”** instead; seed and fertilizer sensors have **“Product application”**.
3. **A parameter** — here **“Pulses”** of the speed sensor.
4. **Its value.** Select the line; the value stands between **−** and **+** and changes with **“MINUS”** / **“PLUS”**.
5. **Scroll bar.** More parameters follow; the last item is **“Reset to defaults”**.

The context menu of the speed sensor at the **“Agronomist”** level.
:::

**“Reset to defaults”** returns the parameters of this sensor to the factory values. It needs the **“Service”** level and acts at once, without asking.

The context menu reached from the [status screen](sensor-status-screen.md) with **“MENU”** has **“Disable control”** or **“Enable control”** as its first item instead of **“Information”** — see [Take a sensor into or out of control](sensor-in-and-out-of-control.md).

## One set for a group, or one per sensor

| **Sensors** | **Settings** |
| --- | --- |
| Seed sensors | One set for all of them. Change it on any seed sensor — it applies to every one. Only **“Product application”** is set per line. |
| Fertilizer sensors | One set for all fertilizer sensors, separate from the seed sensors. **“Product application”** per line. |
| All other sensors | Each sensor has its own settings — set every dispenser, fan or pressure sensor separately. |

## Calibrations

| **What it puts right** | **Where** | **Level** | **Machine** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Travel speed — **“Factor, %”** of the speed sensor, over 100 m. [Calibrate the speed sensor](calibrate-speed.md) | **“Seeding machine parameters”** → **“Speed calibration”**, or the context menu of the speed sensor | Agronomist; from the context menu also Operator with a PIN | drives 100 m |
| Dispenser rotation — **“Wheel, pulses”** against **“Dispenser pulses”**. [Calibrate the dispenser rotation](calibrate-dispenser-rotation.md) | **“Seeding machine parameters”** → **“Dispenser calibration”** | Agronomist | drive wheel turned |
| Dispenser by weight — **“Weight, gr”** and **“Weight, pulses”**. [Calibrate the dispenser by weight](calibrate-dispenser-weight.md) | context menu of the dispenser sensor → **“Dispenser calibration(weight)”** | Operator | standing |
| Dispenser motor by weight. [Calibrate a motor by weight](calibrate-motor-weight.md) | context menu of the motor | Operator | standing |

The two weight calibrations are at the **“Operator”** level because they must be repeated whenever the product changes.

## The kinds of sensor

[Speed sensor](speed-sensor.md) · [Seed and fertilizer sensors](seed-and-fertilizer-sensors.md) · [Dispenser sensor](dispenser-sensor.md) · [Fan sensor](fan-sensor.md) · [Pressure sensor](pressure-sensor.md) · [Hopper and work position sensors](hopper-and-work-position-sensors.md) · [Engine sensors](engine-sensors.md) · [Marker sensors](marker-sensors.md) · [Dispenser motors](motor-context-menu.md)


# The sensor status screen

**“Information”** in the context menu of a sensor opens its status screen ([Sensor settings](sensor-settings.md)). It shows what the panel knows about this one sensor right now — the first place to look when an alarm is not clear.

::: {.anatomy fig="status-speed"}
1. **Channel selector** — which sensor of the whole list this is. **“MINUS”** shows the previous sensor, **“PLUS”** the next; the screen stays open.
2. **“Type:”** — the kind of sensor and its number.
3. **“Unit:”** — where the sensor is connected, here **“Control panel”**. Sensors on the sensor network have no such line.
4. **“Link:”** — the state of the communication. [Table below](#link-states).
5. **The live figure of this kind of sensor** — here the pulse frequency **F=** of the speed sensor, in Hz.
6. **“Min speed, km/h”** in force. **----** means switched off.
7. **“Max speed, km/h”** in force.

The status screen of a speed sensor connected to the panel, machine standing.
:::

At the **“Service”** level a line with the address of the sensor in the sensor network is added at the top. When the sensor has active alarms, two red lines appear at the bottom: **“Alarm 1 from 2”** and the name of the alarm shown.

| **Button** | **Action** |
| --- | --- |
| **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”** | Next / previous sensor. |
| **“UP”** / **“DOWN”** | Next / previous active alarm of this sensor. |
| **“MENU”** | The context menu of this sensor, with **“Disable control”** or **“Enable control”** as first item. At **“Operator”**, while the machine moves, **“MENU”** does nothing on the speed sensor. |
| **“BACK”** | Back to the screen you came from. |

## Link states

| **State** | **Meaning** |
| --- | --- |
| **“Normal”** | The sensor answers. |
| **“Not controlled”** | The sensor is out of control: neither its communication nor anything else is watched. |
| **“No connection”** | The sensor does not answer. Red. |
| **“Wrong device type!”** | Something answers, but not the kind of device the profile expects. Red. |
| **“IMITATION”** | Speed sensor only: the speed is simulated, not measured. Yellow. |

The live figures and the alarms are shown only while the sensor is **under control**, answers, and is of the right kind.

## What each kind of sensor shows

| **Sensor** | **Live figures** |
| --- | --- |
| Speed sensor | **F=** in Hz; with two sensors **F1=** and **F2=**. Then **“Min speed, km/h”** and **“Max speed, km/h”**. With motors that dose by weight, the limits are those the motors can hold, narrowed by the two settings; a limit the settings cannot meet is written in red. |
| Seed and fertilizer sensors | **Status:** and the state of the sensor — [below](#states-of-a-seed-or-fertilizer-sensor). |
| Dispenser sensor | **F=** in Hz, to three decimals. |
| Fan sensor | **F=** in Hz. |
| Pressure sensor | **P=** in kPa. |
| Hopper sensor | **Pin:** with the level on the input, **"0"** or **"1"**. |
| Work position sensor | **“Position: Working”** or **“Position: Transporting”**, and **Pin:** with the level on the input. |
| Ignition, oil pressure, battery charge, fuel level, air filter | **Pin:** with the level on the input. |
| Liquid fertilizer flow sensor | **Status:** **“Working”**, or Working:Tramline in a tramline bout; **Flow=** in L/min. |
| Dispenser motor | **Status:** **“Working”** or **“Faulty”**; after a fault **Last fault:** with the code of the controller. |

## States of a seed or fertilizer sensor

| **Status** | **Meaning** |
| --- | --- |
| **“Working”** | Normal. **Working:Tramline** — normal, in the tramline mode of this bout. |
| **“Configuring”** | The sensor has received new settings from the panel and is applying them. |
| **“Calibration in progress”** | The sensor runs its initial calibration; it takes a few seconds. |
| **“Clogged”** | Something blocks the optical channel — the coulter or seed tube may be blocked. Red. |
| **“Light struck”** | Too much sunlight falls on the sensor; it cannot count. Red. |
| **“Faulty”** | The sensor has failed and must be replaced. Red. |
| **“Unknown”** | Another fault that cannot be identified. Red. |


# Travel speed sensor

Area, rates, skips and doubles are all worked out from the distance travelled. **A speed sensor that is out by a tenth makes every figure on the panel wrong by a tenth.** Set **“Pulses”** and **“Diameter, cm”**, then calibrate ([Calibrate the speed sensor](calibrate-speed.md)) — the calibration sets **“Factor, %”**. The speed sensor cannot be taken out of control.

Open its context menu as in [Sensor settings](sensor-settings.md). Its parameters need the **“Agronomist”** level ([Enable the Agronomist level](enable-agronomist-level.md)).

![The context menu of the speed sensor.](figures/ctx-speed)

**“Speed calibration”**, right under **“Information”**, is shown only while the machine stands. At **“Operator”** it asks for the PIN of a higher level.

| **Parameter** | **What it does** | **Range · default** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **“Pulses”** | Pulses of the sensor per revolution of the shaft it sits on. | 1 … 1000 · 6 |
| **“Count period”** | Over how many of the latest pulse intervals the panel averages the speed. The panel always takes at least 8 and at most 16, none older than two seconds: a higher value gives a steadier but slower figure, values below 8 act as 8. Shown only for a sensor connected to the panel. | 1 … 1000 · 1 |
| **“Diameter, cm”** | Diameter of the drive wheel. | 10 … 200 · 60 |
| **“Factor, %”** | Gear ratio between the wheel and the shaft of the sensor, for a sensor on an intermediate shaft or on the dispenser shaft driven by gears or chain. 100 is a direct 1 : 1 drive. Best left to the calibration. | 1 … 10000 · 100 |
| **“Seeding criteria”** | **“Yes”**: travel is part of the condition under which the panel starts to control the seeding — see [When the panel controls the seeding](seed-and-fertilizer-sensors.md#when-the-panel-controls-the-seeding). **“No”**: the travel speed is left out of that condition — for drills whose speed sensor sits before the clutch. Hidden, and always **“Yes”**, in the **“Precise”** mode and on machines with dispenser motors. | **“No”** / **“Yes”** · **“Yes”** |
| **“Min speed, km/h”** | Below this speed, while the panel is controlling, the speed indicator shows **“FASTER”**. **“No”** switches the check off. | **“No”**, 1 … 99 · **“No”** |
| **“Max speed, km/h”** | Above this speed, while the panel is controlling, the speed indicator shows **“SLOWER”**. **“No”** switches the check off. | **“No”**, 1 … 99 · **“No”** |
| **“Imitation, km/h”** | A simulated speed, to keep working with a faulty sensor. **“No”** = the sensor is used. | **“No”**, 1 … 20 · **“No”** |
| **“Width, cm”** | Distance between the centres of the two wheels. Shown only with **“Input device (2)”** in the profile. | 0 … 10000 · 280 |

The minimum must stay below the maximum: a value that would reach the other limit is not accepted. On a machine with dispenser motors the limits in force are also narrowed to the speeds the motors can dose; if a limit cannot be met, the panel raises **“Error in settings of Min/Max”** ([Speed sensor alarms](alarms-speed-sensor.md)).

## Working out the factor

If you do not calibrate, the factor can be calculated: **k = Na / Nt × 100 %**. Na is the product of the numbers of teeth of all driven gears (the even-numbered ones), Nt the product of the numbers of teeth of all driving gears (the odd-numbered ones), counted from the gear on the shaft of the drive wheel.

If the tractor has a speedometer and the panel shows another speed: **K<sub>new</sub> = K<sub>current</sub> × V<sub>tractor</sub> / V<sub>panel</sub>**.

## Imitation

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **Setting “Imitation, km/h” switches the speed limits off.** **“Min speed, km/h”** and **“Max speed, km/h”** go to **“No”**, and the panel says **“Settings of Min and Max speed switched off!”**. On a machine with dispenser motors it also **locks the product application**: nothing is dosed until you release the lock by holding **“HOME”** ([Lock application by hand](lock-application-by-hand.md)).

With motors the imitated speed is also kept inside the range the dosing allows: a value outside it is pulled to the nearest limit. While the speed is imitated, the link line of the status screen reads **“IMITATION”** in yellow, and the speed indicator shows the imitation sign.

The speed can also come from the built-in GPS receiver. That is switched on in the profile, item **“GPS”**, not here — [The profile](profile.md), [GPS reception](gps-receiver.md).

## The status screen

It shows the pulse frequency **F=** in Hz and the two limits in force — see [The sensor status screen](sensor-status-screen.md).

![The status screen of a speed sensor connected to the panel.](figures/status-speed)


# Calibrate the speed sensor

The calibration measures the distance the panel counts over a marked 100 m and corrects **“Factor, %”** of the speed sensor. Do it before the first seeding and after any change to the wheel or its drive. **Set “Pulses” and “Diameter, cm” first** ([Travel speed sensor](speed-sensor.md)) — the calibration corrects the factor; it cannot replace a wrong pulse figure.

Mark out **100 m** on level ground, as close to field conditions as you can, and put the machine at the start.

## From the Seeding machine parameters

::: steps
1. Raise the level to **“Agronomist”** ([Enable the Agronomist level](enable-agronomist-level.md)).

2. **“Settings”** → **“Seeding machine parameters”**, select **“Speed calibration”** and press **“MENU”**.

   ![The way to the calibration: the Settings menu and the Seeding machine parameters, then the calibration window.](figures/cal-speed-from-menu)

3. The panel shows **“Pass 100m and press MENU”** with a **“STOP”** button. Drive the marked distance and stop at the end.

4. Press **“MENU”** or touch **“STOP”**. The panel shows **“Done”** and closes the window by itself.
:::

## From the context menu of the speed sensor

::: steps
1. Hold **“MENU”** on the home screen, select the speed indicator, press **“MENU”**. The context menu opens.

2. Select **“Speed calibration”** and press **“MENU”**. The item is shown only while the machine stands.

3. At the **“Operator”** level the PIN pad opens: type the PIN of the Agronomist or Service level. At **“Agronomist”** the panel asks **“Are you sure?”** — press **“PLUS”** for **“Yes”**.

   ![The calibration from the context menu: the item, the PIN request at the Operator level, the calibration window.](figures/cal-speed-from-ctx)

4. Go on as in steps 3 and 4 above.
:::

The PIN given here starts this one calibration; the access level stays as it was.

While the calibration runs, product application is locked; it returns to its state before the calibration when the window closes. The panel waits half a second after **“STOP”** and checks the connection to the sensor once more before it takes the result.

## When it does not work

| **The panel shows** | **Meaning** |
| --- | --- |
| **“No speed sensor”** | The profile has no speed sensor. The calibration does not start. |
| **“Connection lost with the sensor! Calibration canceled!”** | The sensor does not answer — at the start, or at the moment of **“STOP”**. |
| **“Sensor not controlled! Calibration canceled!”** | The speed sensor is out of control. |
| **“FAILURE! The tractor did not move!”** | The sensor gave no pulses at all over the distance. Check the sensor, its gap to the target and its cable. |
| **“Calibration canceled!”** | The window was closed with **“BACK”** or a touch outside. Nothing has changed. |
| **“Invalid PIN”** | The PIN asked at the **“Operator”** level was wrong. The calibration does not start. |

If the speed on the panel still differs from the real speed after the calibration, check **“Pulses”** and **“Diameter, cm”** and calibrate again.


# Seed and fertilizer sensors

**The seed sensors share one set of settings**: change it on any seed sensor and it applies to all. The fertilizer sensors share a second set. Only **“Product application”** is set line by line. Open the context menu of any sensor of the group as in [Sensor settings](sensor-settings.md).

![The context menu of a seed sensor.](figures/ctx-seed)

| **Parameter** | **Level** | **What it does** | **Range · default** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **“Product application”** | Agronomist | **“Yes”**: this line sows and is watched. **“No”**: the line is treated as shut off, like a line in a tramline bout — seed through it raises **“Seeding to tramline”**. Not shown when every line of the group has its own motor. | **“No”** / **“Yes”** |
| **“Sensitivity”** | Agronomist | Sensitivity of a seed sensor of an older generation. Shown only when such a sensor is connected. | 1 … 120 · 80 |
| **“Fraction”** | Operator | The count filter of the sensors, set for the size of the seed — a filter against dust and chaff. **Change it with the crop** — [table below](#fraction-for-the-crop). | 1 … 100 · 10 |
| **“Correction”** | Operator | Adapts the sensitivity to the bracket of the sensor. A higher value lowers the sensitivity and keeps dust and fine dirt out of the count. Shown only for the sensor generation that uses it. | 100 … 3300 · 300 |
| **“Rate error,%”** | Agronomist | Permitted deviation of the measured rate from the target; beyond it **“Under allowable rate”** or **“Over allowable rate”**. Only in **“Hybrid”** and **“Precise”**. | 5 … 95 % · 50 % |
| **“Doubles error,%”** | Agronomist | Above this share of doubles: **“High % of doubles”**. **“No”** switches the alarm off. Only in **“Precise”**. | **“No”**, 1 … 95 % · **“No”** |
| **“Skips error,%”** | Agronomist | Above this share of skips: **“High % of skips”**. **“No”** switches the alarm off. Only in **“Precise”**. | **“No”**, 1 … 95 % · **“No”** |
| **“Recalculation,m”** | Operator | The stretch over which skips, doubles and quality are collected for the diagram and the Seeding table. Without a speed sensor it is **“Recalculation,sec”**, in seconds. **“MENU”** on it lets the panel calculate it — [Let the panel calculate the recalculation path](recalculation-path.md). | 10 … 50 · 20 |
| **“Percent of sowing,%”** | Agronomist | The share of sowing lines the panel needs before it starts to control the seeding — [below](#when-the-panel-controls-the-seeding). Seed sensors only; not shown on machines with dispenser motors. | 5 … 80 %, steps of 5 · 20 % |
| **“Toler.sowing to tramline,%”** | Agronomist | How much seed may still pass a line shut off for a tramline, in per cent of the target rate, before **“Seeding to tramline”**. | 0 … 50 % · 20 % |
| **“Group start address”** | Service (seed), Agronomist (fertilizer) | Where the numbering of this group starts in the sensor network. Leave it at **“AUTO”** unless the service tells you otherwise. | **“AUTO”**, … |

In **“Flow”** mode a line is in alarm only when it stays below the alarm level; there is no upper limit. The target rates and alarm levels themselves are set on the home screen — [Change the target rate](set-the-target-rate.md).

## Fraction for the crop

Go by the size of the seed:

| **Crop** | **“Fraction”** |
| --- | --- |
| Rapeseed | 1 – 5 |
| Wheat | 5 – 10 |
| Maize | 10 – 30 |
| Sunflower | 10 – 30 |

On pneumatic drills set **1** whatever the crop. Too high a fraction makes small seeds disappear from the count — the panel then reports too low a rate.

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **Change “Correction” only after talking to the service.** It is needed in rare cases only; a wrong value makes the sensors miss seed or count dust.

## When the panel controls the seeding

The panel starts to watch the seeding — and to raise seed alarms — only when seed flows within the target rate through at least **“Percent of sowing,%”** of the seed lines, and, if **“Seeding criteria”** of the speed sensor is **“Yes”**, the machine moves ([Travel speed sensor](speed-sensor.md)). Until then the diagram shows **“NOT UNDER CONTROL”** — see [Seeding alarms](alarms-seeding.md#not-under-control). With a work position sensor whose **“Alarms criteria”** is **“Yes”**, nothing is watched in the transport position ([Hopper and work position sensors](hopper-and-work-position-sensors.md)).

## The status screen

Shows **Status:** with the state of the sensor — **“Working”**, **“Clogged”**, **“Light struck”** and the others: [The sensor status screen](sensor-status-screen.md#states-of-a-seed-or-fertilizer-sensor).


# Let the panel calculate the recalculation path

**“Recalculation,m”** of the seed sensors is the stretch over which the panel collects skips, doubles and quality before it updates the diagram and the Seeding table ([Seed and fertilizer sensors](seed-and-fertilizer-sensors.md)). A stretch that covers whole turns of the seed disk gives the steadiest figures. The panel can work it out from the target rate in seeds per metre and the number of holes in the disk.

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **Calculate the path again whenever the target rate has changed.** The old path no longer matches whole turns of the disk.

::: steps
1. Set the target rate on the home screen first — [Change the target rate](set-the-target-rate.md). The calculation uses the target of the **“Precise”** mode.

2. Open the context menu of any seed sensor ([Sensor settings](sensor-settings.md)), select **“Recalculation,m”** and press **“MENU”**.

3. **With dispenser motors** the panel asks whether the rate and the number of holes are set — **“Calculate path?”**. Press **“PLUS”** for **“Yes”**. It takes the holes from **“Holes in disk”** of the motor ([The context menu of a motor](motor-context-menu.md)).

   **Without motors** it first reminds you that the seeding rate must already be set; close the message. Then type the number of holes in the disk in the **“Holes in disk”** pad (1 to 500) and touch **“OK”**.

4. The panel calculates the path and sets it: the longest stretch of whole disk turns, up to ten, that fits into 50 m, doubled while it is shorter than 25 m.
:::

If even one turn of the disk is longer than 50 m, the panel shows **“Calculated path to big. Maximum setuped.”** and sets 50 m.

**“No”** in step 3, or **“BACK”** on the pad, leaves the path as it was. You can always set **“Recalculation,m”** by hand with **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”**, from 10 to 50 m.

Without a speed sensor the item is **“Recalculation,sec”** and the stretch is counted in seconds.


# Dispenser shaft sensor

A dispenser shaft sensor counts the turns of the metering shaft. At the least it tells you that the shaft has stopped. Calibrated, it also watches the shaft speed against the travel speed, or counts the weight of product applied. **Each dispenser sensor has its own settings** — set every one.

Open its context menu as in [Sensor settings](sensor-settings.md).

![The context menu of a dispenser shaft sensor.](figures/ctx-dispenser)

| **Parameter** | **Level** | **What it does** | **Range · default** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **“Dispenser calibration(weight)”** | Operator | Starts the calibration by weight — [Calibrate the dispenser by weight](calibrate-dispenser-weight.md). Shown only with **“Weight control”** at **“Yes”**. | — |
| **“Period, s”** | Operator | The longest time between two pulses of the sensor. If the shaft gives no pulse for longer while the machine sows or moves, the panel raises **“No rotation”**. | 1 … 60 s · 10 s |
| **“Rotation speed control”** | Agronomist | **“Yes”**: the shaft speed is watched against the travel speed, within **“Maximum error, %”**. **“No”**: only whether the shaft turns at all. **Needs the rotation calibration.** | **“No”** / **“Yes”** · **“No”** |
| **“Wheel, pulses”** | Agronomist | Pulses of the speed sensor that go with **“Dispenser pulses”** of this sensor. Written by the rotation calibration. Shown with **“Rotation speed control”** at **“Yes”**. | 1 … 65535 · 100 |
| **“Dispenser pulses”** | Agronomist | Pulses of this sensor that go with **“Wheel, pulses”**. Written by the rotation calibration. | 1 … 65535 · 100 |
| **“Maximum error, %”** | Agronomist | Permitted deviation of the shaft speed; beyond it, while the machine moves, **“Low speed of rotation”** or **“High speed of rotation”**. | 1 … 50 % · 10 % |
| **“Weight control”** | Agronomist | **“Yes”**: the panel counts the weight of product applied per hectare from the turns of this shaft. **Needs the calibration by weight.** | **“No”** / **“Yes”** · **“No”** |
| **“Type of product”** | Agronomist | Which product this dispenser applies: **“Product 1”**, **“Product 2”** or **“Product 3”**. Shown with **“Weight control”** at **“Yes”**. | · **“Product 1”** |
| **“Weight, gr”** | Agronomist | Weight of product that goes with **“Weight, pulses”** — together the output of the metering unit per turn. Written by the calibration by weight. | 1 … 65535 · 10000 |
| **“Weight, pulses”** | Agronomist | Pulses of this sensor that go with **“Weight, gr”**. | 1 … 65535 · 100 |

Without a speed sensor in the profile the panel can only watch whether the shaft turns: the speed and weight items are hidden.

## Type of product

The panel follows up to three products by weight. Dispensers that apply the same product get the same number:

| **Machine** | **Setting** |
| --- | --- |
| One dispenser sensor | **“Product 1”**. |
| Two dispensers, the same seed | **“Product 1”** on both. |
| Two dispensers, seed and dry fertilizer | **“Product 1”** on the seed dispenser, **“Product 2”** on the fertilizer dispenser. |
| Three dispensers, two for seed, one for fertilizer | **“Product 1”** on the two seed dispensers, **“Product 2”** on the third. |

A product already dosed by an electric motor cannot be chosen here; the panel skips to the next free one. If no product is free, **“Weight control”** stays at **“No”**.

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **Changing “Type of product”, switching “Weight control” on or off, or taking a weight-controlled dispenser sensor into or out of control can erase the statistics of the active field.** If the field already holds data, the panel asks first — **“Need to erase statistics”** for the active field; **“MENU”** for **“Yes”**, **“BACK”** for **“No”**. To keep the data, select an empty field first ([Start a new field](start-a-new-field.md)).

## The status screen

Shows the pulse frequency **F=** in Hz, to three decimals — [The sensor status screen](sensor-status-screen.md).

![The status screen of a dispenser shaft sensor.](figures/status-dispenser)


# Calibrate the dispenser rotation

With **“Rotation speed control”** at **“Yes”**, a dispenser sensor watches whether the shaft turns as fast as the travel speed demands ([Dispenser shaft sensor](dispenser-sensor.md)). For that the panel must know the ratio between the pulses of the speed sensor and the pulses of the dispenser sensor. The calibration measures it and writes **“Wheel, pulses”** and **“Dispenser pulses”**.

Before you start: the speed sensor and the dispenser sensors to be calibrated must be under control and must answer. You need the **“Agronomist”** level ([Enable the Agronomist level](enable-agronomist-level.md)). Raise the machine so that the drive wheel can be turned, or be ready to move it.

::: steps
1. **“Settings”** → **“Seeding machine parameters”**. Select **“Dispenser calibration”**.

2. Choose with **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”** which dispensers to calibrate: **“ALL”**, or the number of one dispenser.

3. Press **“MENU”**. The **“Calibration”** screen opens with a progress bar at 0 %.

4. Turn the drive wheel. The bar fills as pulses come in from the wheel and from every dispenser being calibrated.

5. At 100 % — at least 100 pulses from each — the panel beeps and shows **“Stop rotation!”**. Stop turning.

6. When no pulse has come for two seconds, the panel stores the values and shows **“Done”**; the **“Seeding machine parameters”** menu returns.
:::

![Dispenser calibration: the menu, the progress while turning, and the message Stop rotation!](figures/cal-dispenser-steps)

**“BACK”** at any moment aborts with **“Calibration canceled!”**; nothing changes.

| **The panel shows** | **Meaning** |
| --- | --- |
| **“Sensor not controlled! Calibration canceled!”** | The speed sensor or a dispenser sensor to be calibrated is out of control. Take it into control ([Take a sensor into or out of control](sensor-in-and-out-of-control.md)). |
| **“Connection lost with the sensor! Calibration canceled!”** | The speed sensor or a dispenser sensor does not answer, at the start or during the calibration. |

The more you turn before **“Stop rotation!”**, the better: the values are scaled down by themselves if the count grows beyond what they can hold.

Calibrate again after any change to the drive between the wheel and the dispenser — sprockets, gearbox or variator.


# Calibrate the dispenser by weight

With **“Weight control”** at **“Yes”**, the panel counts the product applied from the turns of the dispenser shaft ([Dispenser shaft sensor](dispenser-sensor.md)). The calibration measures the weight per pulse and writes **“Weight, gr”** and **“Weight, pulses”**. It is done at the **“Operator”** level, standing.

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **Calibrate again after every change of the metering roller, of the variator or gearbox setting in the dispenser drive, and of the seed in the hopper.** Otherwise the weight shown is wrong.

You need a container, scales and a way to turn the dispenser shaft by hand.

::: steps
1. On the home screen hold **“MENU”**, select the dispenser sensor and press **“MENU”**. The context menu opens.

2. Select **“Dispenser calibration(weight)”** and press **“MENU”**. The calibration screen shows the target rates of the products in use — the product of this dispenser between arrows — and **“PLUS - calibrate dispenser 1”** with the number of the dispenser.

3. Press **“PLUS”**. The panel lists what to do before the calibration: weigh the empty container and write the weight down; fill the hopper; put the empty container under the dispenser; turn the rotor until its cells are filled. Do all of it, then press **“UP”**.

4. The next screen lists the calibration itself and counts the **“Impulses”** from the sensor: empty the container, put it back under the dispenser, and turn the rotor, filling the container — as much as possible, between 2 kg and 60 kg.

5. As soon as more than ten pulses have been counted, the line **“MINUS - complete calibration”** appears. Go on turning until the container holds as much as you can manage — at least 100 pulses and 5 kg give a good result. Then stop.

6. Press **“MINUS”**. The number pad opens: **“Enter the difference of the filled and empty container in grams”**.

7. Weigh the full container, subtract the empty weight, type the difference in grams (2000 to 60000) and touch **“OK”**. The panel stores the values and returns to the first screen.

8. Press **“BACK”** to leave.
:::

![Calibration by weight: the menu item, the first screen, the list before the calibration, the list with the pulse counter, the line MINUS - complete calibration, and the weight entry.](figures/cal-mass-steps)

**“BACK”** on the list before the calibration cancels it. **“BACK”** during the calibration asks **“Are you sure?”** — **“PLUS”** cancels, **“MINUS”** goes on. **“BACK”** on the number pad keeps the old values.

## When it does not start or stops

**“PLUS”** in step 3 works only while the sensor is under control, answers and has no alarm. Otherwise the first screen names the reason — **“Not controlled”**, **“No connection”** or **“FAILURE”**. If the sensor fails during the calibration, the panel shows **“FAILURE”** with the reason; **“BACK”** returns to the first screen.


# Fan sensor

A fan sensor counts the revolutions of the fan of a pneumatic drill or planter. The home screen shows the fan speed in rpm. **Each fan sensor has its own settings.**

Open its context menu as in [Sensor settings](sensor-settings.md).

![The context menu of a fan sensor.](figures/ctx-fan)

| **Parameter** | **Level** | **What it does** | **Range · default** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **“Minimum, rpm”** | Operator | Lowest permitted fan speed. Below it the panel raises **“Low speed of rotation”** — but only while the machine sows, or moves in the working position. | 500 … 9000 rpm, steps of 500 · 3000 |
| **“Maximum, rpm”** | Operator | Highest permitted fan speed. Above it the panel raises **“High speed of rotation”** — at any time, also standing. | 500 … 9000 rpm, steps of 500 · 5000 |
| **“Pulses”** | Agronomist | Pulses of the sensor per revolution of the fan. | 1 … 60 · 2 |

A fan speed that looks right but triggers alarms usually means a wrong **“Pulses”**: twice the pulses show half the speed.

What sowing and moving mean for the panel — [When the panel controls the seeding](seed-and-fertilizer-sensors.md#when-the-panel-controls-the-seeding). Without a speed sensor the minimum is watched while the panel sees seeding. With a work position sensor whose **“Alarms criteria”** is **“Yes”**, the minimum is not watched in the transport position.

## The status screen

Shows the pulse frequency **F=** in Hz — [The sensor status screen](sensor-status-screen.md). The fan speed in rpm is this frequency × 60 ÷ **“Pulses”**.

![The status screen of a fan sensor.](figures/status-fan)

The alarms of the fan and what to check: [Fan or dispenser shaft: speed alarms](alarms-rotation.md).


# Pressure sensor

A pressure sensor measures the vacuum (or overpressure) of the air system — for example at the outlet of the fan or in the seed meters of a vacuum planter. The panel works with the absolute value: **a higher figure means more vacuum.** **Each pressure sensor has its own settings.**

Open its context menu as in [Sensor settings](sensor-settings.md).

![The context menu of a pressure sensor.](figures/ctx-pressure)

| **Parameter** | **Level** | **What it does** | **Range · default** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **“Filter”** | Agronomist | How long the sensor measures and averages the pressure. Raise it if the figure jumps a lot. | 1 … 16 · 1 |
| **“Minimum, Pa”** | Operator | Below this pressure — too little vacuum — the panel raises **“Low pressure”**. **“No”** switches the check off. | **“No”**, 100 … 10000 Pa, steps of 100 · **“No”** |
| **“Maximum, Pa”** | Operator | Above this pressure — too much vacuum — the panel raises **“High pressure”**. **“No”** switches the check off. | **“No”**, 100 … 10000 Pa, steps of 100 · **“No”** |

Both limits are watched only while the machine sows, or moves in the working position — see [When the panel controls the seeding](seed-and-fertilizer-sensors.md#when-the-panel-controls-the-seeding). Without a speed sensor they are watched while the panel sees seeding.

The limits are set in pascals; the status screen shows the pressure in kilopascals: 1 kPa = 1000 Pa.

## The status screen

Shows the measured pressure **P=** in kPa, only while the sensor answers — [The sensor status screen](sensor-status-screen.md).

![The status screen of a pressure sensor that does not answer: the link line is red, no pressure is shown.](figures/status-pressure)

The alarms and what to check: [Pressure alarms](alarms-pressure.md). A new or replaced pressure sensor must first get its address — [Configure a pressure sensor](configure-pressure-sensor.md).


# Hopper and work position sensors

## Hopper level sensor

The hopper sensor reports when the product in the hopper falls below the height at which the sensor is mounted. It has **no settings**: its context menu holds only **“Information”** (and **“Reset to defaults”** at the Service level, which has nothing to reset).

The status screen shows **Pin:** with the level on its input: **"1"** — the hopper is empty at the sensor, and the panel raises **“Hopper empty”**; **"0"** — product covers the sensor. See [Hopper alarms](alarms-hopper.md).

## Work position sensor

The work position sensor tells the panel whether the implement is lowered in the **working position** or raised in the **transport position**. Open its context menu as in [Sensor settings](sensor-settings.md).

![The context menu of the work position sensor.](figures/ctx-workpos)

| **Parameter** | **Level** | **What it does** | **Values · default** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **“Transporting position signal”** | Agronomist | The level on the input that means **transport position**: **0** or **1**. Set it to what the sensor gives with the implement raised. | 0 / 1 · 0 |
| **“Alarms criteria”** | Agronomist | **“Yes”**: in the transport position the panel does not watch the seeding, and the fan minimum, the pressure limits and the dispenser shafts are not watched on the move — no alarms at the headland. **“No”**: the position is only shown; it does not affect the alarms. Hidden, and always **“Yes”**, on machines with dispenser motors or a liquid pump controller. | **“No”** / **“Yes”** · **“Yes”** |

On a machine with dispenser motors, a work position sensor that does not answer counts as **transport position** — for safety, nothing is dosed. Without motors, a sensor that does not answer or is out of control counts as working position.

The status screen shows **“Position: Working”** or **“Position: Transporting”**, and **Pin:** with the level on the input — compare it with the real position when you set **“Transporting position signal”**. The position changes after a short filter, so a bump does not toggle it.

![The status screen of the work position sensor.](figures/status-workpos)

On the home screen the implement indicator blinks yellow in the transport position — see [Indicators](indicators.md).


# Engine sensors of the fan drive

Drills whose fan is driven by its own engine can watch that engine with up to five switch sensors on an input device. Each is entered in the [profile](profile.md) on its own. All five have the same two settings and the same status screen; they differ in what the signal means.

![The context menu of the ignition sensor.](figures/ctx-ignition)

| **Parameter** | **Level** | **What it does** | **Range · default** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **“Activation signal”** | Agronomist | The level on the input, **0** or **1**, that means the state in the table below. | 0 / 1 · 1 |
| **“Signal delay, sec”** | Agronomist | How long the input must hold its new level before the panel accepts the change — against false triggering from vibration or a loose contact. | 1 … 30 s · 1 s; **“Low fuel”** 15 s, **“Air filter”** 5 s |

| **Sensor** | **The activation signal means** | **Alarm** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **“Ignition”** | The ignition of the fan-drive engine is switched on. | none — see below |
| **“Emergency oil pressure”** | The oil pressure of the engine is too low. | yes, only with the ignition on |
| **“No battery charge”** | The battery is not being charged by the engine. | yes, only with the ignition on |
| **“Low fuel”** | Little fuel is left in the tank of the engine. | yes |
| **“Air filter”** | The air filter of the engine is dirty. | yes |

The defaults of **“Signal delay, sec”** for **“Low fuel”** and **“Air filter”** are set when the sensor is reset to its defaults.

## How the ignition sensor gates the others

The ignition sensor raises no alarm of its own. It keeps the oil pressure and battery charge sensors quiet while the engine is off — with the ignition off, low oil pressure and no charging are normal. While the ignition sensor is under control, answers and signals the ignition off, these two stay quiet. If the ignition sensor is out of control or does not answer, they report whatever the state of the ignition.

That is why **“Emergency oil pressure”** and **“No battery charge”** should be in the profile only together with **“Ignition”**, and be taken out together with it.

On the home screen the ignition indicator is yellow while the ignition is off and grey while it is on — see [Indicators](indicators.md).

## The status screen

Shows **Pin:** with the present level on the input, **"0"** or **"1"** — compare it with the real state of the engine to set **“Activation signal”**. See [The sensor status screen](sensor-status-screen.md).

![The status screen of the ignition sensor.](figures/status-ignition)

The alarms and what to check: [Engine alarms](alarms-engine.md).


# Marker sensors

Marker sensors tell the panel whether the marker arms are up or down. The home screen draws the two arms; both up are shown yellow — see [Indicators](indicators.md#markers). How many sensors watch the arms is set under **“Markers”** in the [profile](profile.md): **“One”** or **“Both”**.

Open the context menu of a marker sensor as in [Sensor settings](sensor-settings.md). Both settings need the **“Agronomist”** level.

| **Parameter** | **What it does** | **Values · default** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **“Connected marker”** | Which arm the single sensor watches: **“Left”** or **“Right”**. Shown only with **“Markers”** at **“One”**. | · **“Left”** |
| **“Signal "down"”** | The level on the input, **0** or **1**, that means the arm is down. Set it to what the sensor gives with the arm lowered. | 0 / 1 · 0 |

The status screen of a marker sensor shows only the common lines — type, link and alarms ([The sensor status screen](sensor-status-screen.md)).
