A marker sensor raises only the alarms every device can raise: **“Connection lost”** and **“Wrong device type!”** — see [Device does not answer](alarms-any-device.md).


# Device configuration

Every device on the sensor network answers on its own **address**. A seed sensor's address is the number of its row. A new or replaced sensor must get the right address before the panel can find it. This is **device configuration**, in **“Service”** → **“Sensors Configuration”**.

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **This work is for commissioning and for replacing a seed or fertilizer sensor.** It is mostly done at the factory or by an authorised service engineer. A wrong address makes a sensor answer in the place of another. Do not try out unknown items of the **“Service”** menu; follow only this manual or the service engineer of Agriwelt GmbH.

## Prepare

::: steps
1. Disconnect all sensors from the cable entry of the communication harness on the panel — the four-pin connector.

   ![The cable entry of the communication harness: the four-pin connector, the harness and the power connection.](figures/cable-entry)

2. Connect **only** the device that is to get a new address.

3. Switch the panel on. When it has started, it reports **“Connection lost”** for all the devices that are missing. Close the windows with **“HOME”**.

4. Raise the level to **“Agronomist”** — [Enable the Agronomist level](enable-agronomist-level.md). For a HUB-8 concentrator or a tramline actuator raise it to **“Service”**.

5. Press **“BACK”** to return to the main menu. Select **“Service”** and press **“MENU”**.

6. Select **“Sensors Configuration”** and press **“MENU”**. The menu lists the devices that can be configured.

   ![The way to the sensor configuration: Settings, the main menu, the Service menu, the Sensors Configuration menu.](figures/menu-to-sensorconfig)
:::

| **Item** | **Level** | **How** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **“Seed sensor”** | Agronomist | [Configure a seed sensor](configure-seed-sensor.md) |
| **“Pressure sensor”** | Agronomist | [Configure a pressure sensor](configure-pressure-sensor.md) |
| **“HUB8”** | Service | [Configure a HUB-8 concentrator](configure-hub8.md) |
| **“Tramline actuator”** | Service | For the service engineer only. |

## The rules of every configuration

- **One device on the harness.** With **“Sensor address”** at **“AUTO”** the panel takes the one device it finds. If more than one answers, it refuses with **“More than one device in network!”**; if none answers, it shows **“No connection”**.
- **The new address must be free.** When the device was picked by its present address instead of **“AUTO”**, the panel also checks the new one: if another device already uses it, it shows **“Address: … is used!”** with the number, and changes nothing.
- **Any other refusal** reads **“Error #”** with a number. Disconnect and connect the device, and try again.
- **Check the result**: disconnect the device, connect it again, and return to the home screen with **“BACK”**. The device must appear in its place, without a red cross.

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **When all devices are done, return to “Operator”** — set **“User”** back in the **“Settings”** menu, or switch the panel off and on. Then reconnect all devices.


# Configure a seed sensor

For a seed sensor the new address is **the number of its row** — the number shown under its column on the home screen. Prepare first as in [Device configuration](device-configuration.md): only this sensor on the harness, **“Agronomist”** level, **“Sensors Configuration”** menu open.

The address of a seed sensor can be changed only while the sensor **works normally**. A tube sensor is ready as soon as it is connected. An **open** sensor must sit on its coulter, or be held so that **no direct light falls into the optical channel** — the gap between the two glasses. In direct light the sensor reports a fault and does not take the new address.

![Holding an open seed sensor: a finger covers the optical channel between the glasses.](figures/sensor-orientation)

::: steps
1. In **“Sensors Configuration”** select **“Seed sensor”** and press **“MENU”**. The menu has three items: **“Sensor address”**, **“New address”** and **“Set”**.

2. Leave **“Sensor address”** at **“AUTO”**. If it shows something else, set it back with **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”**.

3. Select **“New address”** and set the row number with **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”**.

4. Select **“Set”** and press **“MENU”**. The panel answers **“Done”** and the address it found the sensor on.

5. Disconnect the sensor and connect it again. Return to the home screen with **“BACK”** (twice from the **“Service”** menu). The sensor must appear under its row; the rows not plugged in show a red cross.

   ![The home screen after re-addressing, with only one sensor on the harness: the other rows and devices crossed out in red.](figures/home-after-readdress)
:::

Repeat for every sensor to be addressed. When all are done, return to **“Operator”** — set **“User”** back in **“Settings”**, or switch the panel off and on — and reconnect all devices.

## Searching for a sensor

**Hold “MENU”** on **“Sensor address”** to search the network for a seed sensor: the item then shows the present address of the sensor found. Hold **“MENU”** again to search for the next one. With a found address in place of **“AUTO”**, **“Set”** re-addresses exactly that sensor, and the panel checks that the new address is free. If nothing is found, the panel shows **“No connection”**.

What the error messages mean: [The rules of every configuration](device-configuration.md#the-rules-of-every-configuration).


# Configure a pressure sensor

Each pressure sensor of the profile answers on its own address; the first pressure sensor has the first address of the range, the second the next, and so on. **“New address”** offers only the addresses of that range. Ask the service which one your sensor needs if you are not sure. Prepare first as in [Device configuration](device-configuration.md): only this sensor on the harness, **“Agronomist”** level, **“Sensors Configuration”** menu open.

::: steps
1. In **“Sensors Configuration”** select **“Pressure sensor”** and press **“MENU”**. The menu has three items: **“Sensor address”**, **“New address”** and **“Set”**.

2. Leave **“Sensor address”** at **“AUTO”**.

3. Select **“New address”** and set the address with **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”**. It opens at the first address of the range, the one of pressure sensor 1.

4. Select **“Set”** and press **“MENU”**. The panel answers **“Done”**.

   ![The Pressure sensor menu (the address is covered in this manual).](figures/addr-pressure)

5. Disconnect the sensor and connect it again. Return to the home screen with **“BACK”**. The pressure sensor must report back; while a pressure sensor is missing, its indicator shows a red cross and **XXXX**.

   ![The home screen while the pressure sensors are not plugged in.](figures/home-pressure-offline)
:::

When all devices are done, return to **“Operator”** — set **“User”** back in **“Settings”**, or switch the panel off and on — and reconnect all devices.

**Hold “MENU”** on **“Sensor address”** to search for a pressure sensor on the harness, as described for the seed sensor — [Searching for a sensor](configure-seed-sensor.md#searching-for-a-sensor). The error messages: [The rules of every configuration](device-configuration.md#the-rules-of-every-configuration).


# Configure a HUB-8 concentrator

A HUB-8 concentrator collects up to eight sensors and stands, on the sensor network, in for each of them: every channel appears to the panel as an **input device** or as a **seed sensor** with its own address. The configuration tells each channel what it stands in for and which one it is in its group. It needs the **“Service”** level. Prepare first as in [Device configuration](device-configuration.md): only the concentrator on the harness, **“Sensors Configuration”** menu open.

::: steps
1. In **“Sensors Configuration”** select **“HUB8”** and press **“MENU”**. The menu shows **“Device address”**, then for each channel a pair **“Channel 1 type”** and **“Channel 1 address”**, up to channel 8, and **“Set”** at the end.

2. Leave **“Device address”** at **“AUTO”**.

3. Select **“Channel 1 type”** and choose with **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”** what the channel stands in for: **“Input device”** or **“Seed sensors”**.

4. Select **“Channel 1 address”** and set with **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”** which device of its group this channel is — its sequence number among the input devices or among the seed sensors.

5. Do the same for channels 2 to 8.

6. Select **“Set”** and press **“MENU”**. The panel answers **“Done”**.

7. Disconnect the concentrator and connect it again. Return to the home screen with **“BACK”**. The devices on its channels must report back; while the concentrator is unplugged, they are crossed out in red.

   ![The home screen while the concentrator is unplugged: dispensers, fan and pressure sensors crossed out.](figures/home-after-hub8)
:::

When all devices are done, return to **“Operator”** — set **“User”** back in **“Settings”**, or switch the panel off and on — and reconnect all devices.

## Shortcuts

- **Hold “MENU”** on one of **“Channel 1 type”** to **“Channel 8 type”**: all the following channels get the same type, and their addresses are numbered on from this channel.
- **Hold “MENU”** on one of **“Channel 1 address”** to **“Channel 8 address”**: the following channels of the same type are numbered on from this one.
- **Hold “MENU”** on **“Device address”**: the panel searches for a concentrator and reads its present channel settings into the menu. Hold it again for the next one.

When you change a channel type, the address of that channel jumps to the first free one of the new type. If two channels of the same type end up with the same address, **“Set”** refuses with **“Invalid profile!”**. The other messages: [The rules of every configuration](device-configuration.md#the-rules-of-every-configuration).


# How alarms work

An alarm is a window that opens over the working screen, with an alarm signal. It tells you that one device — a sensor, a motor, an actuator — or the system as a whole has found a fault. The alarm topics of this section are grouped by device. **Look for the words you see on the screen.**

## When the panel raises an alarm

A fault is not reported the moment it appears. **The condition must hold without a break for the time set in “Alarm delay” before the window opens.**

| **Setting** | **Value** |
| --- | --- |
| Where | **“Settings”** → **“Alarm delay”**, **“Operator”** level — [The Settings menu](settings-menu.md) |
| Range | 2 to 20 seconds, in steps of 1 second |
| Default | 3 seconds. A stored value outside the range is reset to 3 by itself. |

A short delay reacts fast, but also to a single bump or a short gap in the seed flow. A long delay keeps the screen quiet, but a real fault can run for up to twenty seconds before you hear of it.

> **TIP**
>
> **If the system alarms too often on a rough field, raise “Alarm delay” first.** Change the sensor settings only if a longer delay does not help.

Two cases do not follow the delay:

- **A lost connection** is counted in polls: **“Connection lost”** appears after **three polls in a row** without an answer.
- **Right after a sensor has received new settings**, its alarms are held back for a short time, so that configuring a device does not cause a burst of alarms.

## The alarm window

::: {.anatomy fig="alarm-window"}
1. **“FAILURE!”** — the red title of every alarm window, whatever the fault.
2. **“HOME - close message”** — the hint how to close it.
3. **The alarm text** — the fault. Look it up under this text in the alarm topics.
4. **The kind of device**, here the fan. The same text can come from different devices; this line tells you which.
5. **The number of the device**, here fan 1. When several devices of one kind report the same fault, they share one window and are listed together, for example **#3-5,8**.
6. **“Close”** — closes this alarm.

The alarm window of a fan sensor that does not answer.
:::

The alarms of the system as a whole — for example about the rate of a product — have no device line.

## Closing an alarm

| **What you do** | **What happens** |
| --- | --- |
| Press **“HOME”**, or touch **“Close”** | This alarm closes. If more alarms are waiting, the next one opens. The other buttons do nothing in the window. |
| Hold **“HOME”** | The window closes and the panel returns to the home screen. |

While the window is open, the panel sounds the alarm signal and lights its alarm indicator. **Closing a window does not repair the fault**, and the same alarm comes back only after the fault has cleared and appeared again. The active alarms of a sensor stay listed on its status screen — [The sensor status screen](sensor-status-screen.md).

## Alarms are hidden at the higher access levels

At **“Agronomist”** and **“Service”** no alarm windows are shown. They are not lost: when you return to **“Operator”**, the panel drops the alarms that have cleared and shows the ones that are still true. See [Access levels](access-levels.md#what-happens-to-the-alarms-while-the-level-is-high) and [User is Agronomist](alarms-access-level.md).

## Not alarm windows

| **Message** | **Where** | **Topic** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **“SLOWER”**, **“FASTER”** | in place of the speed figure | [Speed sensor alarms](alarms-speed-sensor.md) |
| **“NOT UNDER CONTROL”** | on the seed diagram | [Seeding alarms](alarms-seeding.md#not-under-control) |

## The alarm topics

[Any device](alarms-any-device.md) · [Speed sensor](alarms-speed-sensor.md) · [Seeding](alarms-seeding.md) · [Seed sensor state](alarms-sensor-state.md) · [Fan and dispenser shaft](alarms-rotation.md) · [Hopper](alarms-hopper.md) · [Pressure](alarms-pressure.md) · [Engine](alarms-engine.md) · [Dosing by weight](alarms-dosing-by-weight.md) · [Access level](alarms-access-level.md) · [Tramline](alarms-tramline.md) · [Dispenser motors](alarms-electric-motors.md)

Each alarm has its own heading with the text exactly as on the screen. Under it: what the panel has found, and what to check, in the order a mechanic checks it — the quick checks on the panel first, then the machine, then the sensor itself.

> **NOTE**
>
> If the checks do not clear the fault, call the service. The contact details are in the data sheet of the system.


# Device does not answer: Connection lost, Wrong device type!

Every device on the sensor network can raise these two alarms. **The device line of the alarm window tells you which one** — see [How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md).

## “Connection lost”

**What it means.** The device has not answered three polls in a row. The panel no longer knows its state: nothing about it is watched until it answers again. Its indicator shows a red cross or **XXXX**; its status screen shows **“No connection”**.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. Was the device recently added to the profile? Then it may not have its address yet — [Device configuration](device-configuration.md).
2. The connectors of the device and of the harness: plugged in fully, pins clean and straight, no water inside.
3. The cable of the device and the harness: crushed, chafed or torn, especially at hinges and folding points.
4. The power supply of the device. It must match the values in the data sheet of the system.
5. The profile: does it list a device that the machine does not have? — [Check the profile and the connections](check-profile-and-connections.md).
6. The device itself: swap it with a device of the same kind that works. If the fault moves with it, the device is faulty.

When several devices of one kind are lost at once, look first at what they share: one input device, one HUB-8 concentrator, one branch of the harness.

## “Wrong device type!”

**What it means.** Something answers on the address of this device, but not the kind of device the profile expects there — for example an input device where a pressure sensor should be.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The profile: the kind of each device as installed — [The profile](profile.md).
2. Was a device replaced or re-addressed recently? Two devices may now share an address, or one has the address meant for another. Address it again — [Device configuration](device-configuration.md).
3. On a HUB-8 concentrator: the type of each channel — [Configure a HUB-8 concentrator](configure-hub8.md).

If you have to keep working with a device that does not answer, you can take it out of control until it is repaired — [Take a sensor into or out of control](sensor-in-and-out-of-control.md). It is then not watched at all.


# Travel speed: SLOWER, FASTER and speed sensor alarms

The travel speed outside its limits raises **no alarm window**. The speed indicator on the home screen shows **“SLOWER”** or **“FASTER”** instead of the figure, as long as the speed is wrong — see [Indicators](indicators.md#speed). The limits are **“Min speed, km/h”** and **“Max speed, km/h”** of the speed sensor ([Travel speed sensor](speed-sensor.md)); they are watched only while the panel is controlling the seeding.

## “SLOWER”

**What it means.** The machine moves faster than **“Max speed, km/h”** permits.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. Drive slower.
2. The speed on the panel matches the real speed — compare with the tractor or a GPS.
3. The settings of the speed sensor: **“Pulses”**, **“Diameter, cm”**, **“Factor, %”**, **“Max speed, km/h”**.
4. Calibrate the speed sensor — [Calibrate the speed sensor](calibrate-speed.md).
5. The speed sensor itself is serviceable.

## “FASTER”

**What it means.** The machine moves slower than **“Min speed, km/h”** permits.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. Drive faster.
2. The speed on the panel matches the real speed.
3. The settings of the speed sensor, including **“Min speed, km/h”**.
4. Calibrate the speed sensor.
5. The speed sensor itself is serviceable.

While the speed is imitated, the indicator shows **“INCREASE IMITATION”** or **“DECREASE IMITATION”** instead: change **“Imitation, km/h”**.

## “Speed sensor #1 failed” / “Speed sensor #2 failed”

**What it means.** Only with two speed sensors on an input device (**“Input device (2)”** in the profile): the machine moves, but this sensor has given no pulse for too long.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The gap between the sensor and its target, and the target itself.
2. The connector and cable of the sensor up to the input device.
3. The sensor itself — swap the two sensors; if the fault moves, the sensor is faulty.

## “Error in settings of Min/Max”

**What it means.** On a machine whose motors dose by weight: a speed limit set on the speed sensor cannot be met together with the speeds the motors can dose at — the minimum lies at or above the highest dosing speed, or the maximum at or below the lowest.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The status screen of the speed sensor: it shows the limits in force and writes the impossible one in red — [The sensor status screen](sensor-status-screen.md).
2. **“Min speed, km/h”** and **“Max speed, km/h”** of the speed sensor.
3. The target rates of the products and the speed limits of the motors — [Calibrate a motor by weight](calibrate-motor-weight.md).


# Seeding alarms: rate, skips, doubles, NOT UNDER CONTROL

These alarms come from the seed sensors and the fertilizer sensors. **The device line tells you which line** — for example **Seed sensor: #4**. The limits are the settings of the group ([Seed and fertilizer sensors](seed-and-fertilizer-sensors.md)). Check the speed first in every case: a wrong travel speed makes every rate per metre wrong.

## NOT UNDER CONTROL

**What it means.** Not an alarm window: the seed diagram shows **“NOT UNDER CONTROL”**. Seed flows, but not through enough lines to meet the condition for control — fewer than **“Percent of sowing,%”** of the seed lines sow within the target. Until the condition is met the panel watches no seeding fault.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The speed on the panel matches the real speed.
2. The target rate — in **“Flow”** the alarm level — on the home screen: is it far above what the machine really sows? — [Change the target rate](set-the-target-rate.md).
3. **“Fraction”** of the seed sensors — too high a value hides small seeds.
4. Enough seed in the hoppers.

## “Under allowable rate”

**What it means.** A line sows less than permitted: in **“Flow”** below the alarm level, in **“Hybrid”** and **“Precise”** below the target by more than **“Rate error,%”**.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The speed on the panel matches the real speed.
2. Enough seed in the hoppers.
3. The metering unit works and is set right.
4. **“Fraction”** of the sensors — it may have to be lowered.
5. The sensor itself — its state on the status screen ([The sensor status screen](sensor-status-screen.md#states-of-a-seed-or-fertilizer-sensor)).

## “Over allowable rate”

**What it means.** A line sows more than the target plus **“Rate error,%”**. Only in **“Hybrid”** and **“Precise”**.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The speed on the panel matches the real speed.
2. The metering unit works and is set right.
3. **“Fraction”** of the sensors — it may have to be raised.
4. The sensor itself — its state on the status screen.

## “High % of doubles”

**What it means.** The share of doubles over the last stretch is above **“Doubles error,%”**. Only in **“Precise”**, and only if that setting is not **“No”**.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The speed on the panel matches the real speed.
2. **“Doubles error,%”** of the seed sensors.
3. The metering unit: vacuum, singulator, disk for the seed.
4. **“Fraction”** — it may have to be raised.
5. The sensor itself — its state on the status screen.

## “High % of skips”

**What it means.** The share of skips over the last stretch is above **“Skips error,%”**. Only in **“Precise”**, and only if that setting is not **“No”**.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The speed on the panel matches the real speed.
2. **“Skips error,%”** of the seed sensors.
3. Enough seed in the hoppers.
4. The metering unit: vacuum, singulator, disk for the seed.
5. **“Fraction”** — it may have to be lowered.
6. The sensor itself — its state on the status screen.

## “Seeding to tramline”

**What it means.** A line that should be shut off — in a tramline bout, or with **“Product application”** at **“No”** — passes more seed than **“Toler.sowing to tramline,%”** of the target rate.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The tramline actuator of that line shuts off — see [Tramline alarms](alarms-tramline.md).
2. The setting **“Relation of sensors to actuators”** — the right lines assigned to the actuator ([Seeding machine parameters](seeding-machine-parameters.md)).
3. **“Toler.sowing to tramline,%”**.

## “Old firmware! Wrong S&D calc!”

**What it means.** A fertilizer sensor running in **“Precise”** has firmware too old to count skips and doubles correctly.

**What to check:** run the fertilizer sensors in **“Flow”** or **“Hybrid”**, or have the sensor replaced or updated by the service.


# Seed sensor state: Clogged, Light struck, Broken

These three alarms are reported by the seed or fertilizer sensor itself about its own state. The device line names the sensor. Its status screen shows the same state in the line **Status:** — [The sensor status screen](sensor-status-screen.md#states-of-a-seed-or-fertilizer-sensor).

## “Clogged”

**What it means.** Something blocks the optical channel of the sensor. The coulter or the seed tube may be blocked.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The coulter and the seed tube: soil, a stone, wet seed.
2. The optical channel of the sensor: remove the blockage, clean off dust.
3. The power supply of the sensor — it must match the values in the data sheet of the system.

## “Light struck”

**What it means.** Too much light falls into the optical channel; the sensor cannot count. The panel reports it only while the machine moves (or always, without a speed sensor) — a raised implement at the headland does not cause it.

**What to check:** keep direct sunlight out of the optical channel — the seat of an open sensor on its coulter, the covers, the position of the sensor.

## “Broken”

**What it means.** The sensor has detected a fault in itself. On its status screen it reads **“Faulty”**. The sensor may have to be replaced.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The power supply of the sensor — it must match the values in the data sheet of the system.
2. Disconnect and connect the sensor.
3. If it stays **“Faulty”**, replace the sensor. A new seed sensor needs the number of its row — [Configure a seed sensor](configure-seed-sensor.md).


# Fan or dispenser shaft: speed alarms

The fan sensor and the dispenser shaft sensor use the same two messages. **The device line of the alarm window tells you which one** — **Fan** or **Dispenser**, with its number. How the window works: [How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md).

## “Low speed of rotation”

**What it means.** The fan turns slower than **“Minimum, rpm”**, or the dispenser shaft slower than the travel speed demands, by more than **“Maximum error, %”**.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. **Dispenser only:** the speed on the panel matches the real speed.
2. The component being watched — the fan and its drive, or the dispenser and its drive.
3. The settings of the sensor: for the fan **“Minimum, rpm”** and **“Pulses”** — [Fan sensor](fan-sensor.md); for the dispenser **“Maximum error, %”** — [Dispenser shaft sensor](dispenser-sensor.md).
4. The sensor itself is serviceable.
5. **Dispenser only:** calibrate the rotation again — [Calibrate the dispenser rotation](calibrate-dispenser-rotation.md).

## “High speed of rotation”

**What it means.** The fan turns faster than **“Maximum, rpm”** — this is watched also when the machine stands — or the dispenser shaft faster than the travel speed demands, by more than **“Maximum error, %”**.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. **Dispenser only:** the speed on the panel matches the real speed.
2. The component being watched — the fan and its drive, or the dispenser and its drive.
3. The settings of the sensor: for the fan **“Maximum, rpm”** and **“Pulses”**; for the dispenser **“Maximum error, %”**.
4. The sensor itself is serviceable.
5. **Dispenser only:** calibrate the rotation again.

The dispenser shaft speed is watched only with **“Rotation speed control”** at **“Yes”**, and only while the machine moves.

## “No rotation”

**What it means.** The dispenser shaft gives no pulse for longer than **“Period, s”** while the machine sows or moves. Only the dispenser shaft sensor raises this alarm.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The dispenser and its drive — chain, clutch, shear pin.
2. **“Period, s”** of the sensor: long enough for the slowest shaft speed at work — [Dispenser shaft sensor](dispenser-sensor.md).
3. The gap between the sensor and its target, and the sensor itself.


# Hopper empty

The hopper level sensor sits at a fixed height in the hopper. The device line names the hopper: **Hopper: #2**. On the home screen the hopper indicator turns red — see [Indicators](indicators.md#hopper).

## “Hopper empty”

**What it means.** The product in the hopper has fallen below the height of the sensor.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. Fill the hopper.
2. If the product is above the sensor and the alarm stays: product bridging or caked on the sensor — clean the sensor.
3. The status screen of the sensor: **Pin:** reads **"1"** while the panel sees the hopper empty — [Hopper and work position sensors](hopper-and-work-position-sensors.md).
4. The sensor itself is serviceable.

The hopper sensor has no settings; an alarm that does not match the hopper is a matter of the sensor, its mounting height or its cable.


# Pressure alarms: High pressure, Low pressure

The panel compares the absolute value of the measured pressure with **“Minimum, Pa”** and **“Maximum, Pa”** of the sensor ([Pressure sensor](pressure-sensor.md)), while the machine sows or moves in the working position. The device line names the sensor: **Pressure sensor: #1**.

## “High pressure”

**What it means.** The measured pressure is above **“Maximum, Pa”** — too much vacuum.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. Lower the speed of the fan or turbine.
2. The damper of the air intake, if the machine has one.
3. The tube to the pressure sensor: connected at the right point, not kinked, not blocked.
4. **“Maximum, Pa”** of the sensor.

## “Low pressure”

**What it means.** The measured pressure is below **“Minimum, Pa”** — too little vacuum.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. Raise the speed of the fan or turbine.
2. The damper of the air intake, if the machine has one.
3. The air ducts and meters for leaks — hoses, seals, covers.
4. The tube to the pressure sensor: connected at the right point, not kinked, not blocked.
5. **“Minimum, Pa”** of the sensor.

The measured pressure is on the status screen of the sensor, **P=** in kPa — compare it with the limits, which are set in Pa (1 kPa = 1000 Pa).


# Engine alarms: oil pressure, battery charge, fuel, air filter

The sensors of a separate fan-drive engine all raise the same alarm text, **“FAILURE”**. **The device line names the sensor** — that line is what you look up here. The settings of these sensors: [Engine sensors of the fan drive](engine-sensors.md).

The ignition sensor raises no alarm. It keeps the oil pressure and battery charge alarms quiet while the ignition is off.

## “Emergency oil pressure”

**What it means.** The low oil pressure sensor of the engine has triggered — with the ignition on, if there is an ignition sensor.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. Stop the engine and check the oil level and the oil pressure.
2. The oil pressure sensor is serviceable.
3. **“Activation signal”** of the oil pressure sensor: compare **Pin:** on its status screen with the real state.
4. If the alarm comes with the engine off: is the ignition sensor in the profile and under control? Is it serviceable?

## “No battery charge”

**What it means.** The battery is not being charged by the engine — with the ignition on, if there is an ignition sensor.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The alternator, its belt and the charging circuit of the engine.
2. The battery charge sensor is serviceable.
3. **“Activation signal”** of the battery charge sensor.
4. If the alarm comes with the engine off: is the ignition sensor in the profile and under control? Is it serviceable?

## “Low fuel”

**What it means.** Little fuel is left in the tank of the engine.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. Refuel.
2. The fuel level sensor is serviceable.
3. **“Activation signal”** of the fuel level sensor.
4. **“Signal delay, sec”** — fuel slopping in the tank on rough ground can trigger it; the default is 15 seconds.

## “Air filter”

**What it means.** The air filter of the engine is dirty.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. Clean or replace the air filter.
2. The air filter sensor is serviceable.
3. **“Activation signal”** of the air filter sensor.
4. **“Signal delay, sec”** — the default is 5 seconds.


# Dosing by weight: product rate too low or too high

These are alarms of the system as a whole: the window has no device line. They come only when a product is followed by weight — by a dispenser shaft sensor with **“Weight control”** at **“Yes”**, or by dispenser motors. The number in the text is the number of the product, **“Product 1”** to **“Product 3”**.

## “Rate of Product 1 is to low!” / “Rate of Product 1 is to high!”

**What it means.** The weight of the product applied per hectare deviates from its target rate by more than **“Product rate error,%”** of the **“Settings”** menu ([The Settings menu](settings-menu.md)).

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The target rate of the product — [Change the target rate](set-the-target-rate.md).
2. The metering unit: roller, variator or gearbox setting, product flow from the hopper.
3. The settings of the dispenser shaft sensor that applies this product, and its **“Type of product”** — [Dispenser shaft sensor](dispenser-sensor.md).
4. The dispenser shaft sensor is serviceable.
5. Calibrate by weight again — [Calibrate the dispenser by weight](calibrate-dispenser-weight.md), or for motors [Calibrate a motor by weight](calibrate-motor-weight.md). A new roller, another setting of the drive or another seed always need a new calibration.

## “Product dosage is impossible! Check product rate and calibration!”

**What it means.** On a machine with dispenser motors: with the present target rates and calibrations no travel speed exists at which the motors could apply all products. The panel shows it again each time the seeding starts.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The target rates of the products.
2. The calibration of the motors and their shaft speed limits — [Calibrate a motor by weight](calibrate-motor-weight.md).


# User is Agronomist! Alarms will not be shown!

At the **“Agronomist”** and **“Service”** levels the panel shows no alarm windows ([Access levels](access-levels.md)). This one is the exception.

## “User is Agronomist! Alarms will not be shown!”

**What it means.** The panel sees seeding while the access level is **“Agronomist”** or **“Service”**. It warns you once that no seeding faults will be reported. The message comes only once for the whole time the higher level stays set; it comes again after you have gone down to **“Operator”** and up again.

**What to do:** set the level back to **“Operator”** before you work — in **“Settings”** set **“User”** to **“Operator”** and press **“MENU”**, or switch the panel off and on. The alarms that are still true are then shown one after another.

> **WARNING**
>
> **Do not sow at the Agronomist level.** A blocked coulter, an empty hopper or a stopped fan stays unreported for the whole field.


# Tramline alarms: Illegal state, Stall

A tramline actuator shuts off the seed lines of the tramline on the bouts the rhythm asks for ([Next tramline bout](next-tramline-bout.md)). The device line names it: **Tramline actuator: #1**.

## “Illegal state”

**What it means.** The actuator reports both end positions at the same time — pulled in and pulled out. Its end position switches contradict each other.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The end position switches of the actuator and their wiring.
2. Dirt or ice holding a switch.
3. The actuator itself.

## “Stall”

**What it means.** The actuator was told to move but has not reached the position asked for.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The shutter: blocked by seed, dirt or a bent part.
2. The power supply of the actuator.
3. The end position switch of the position asked for.
4. The actuator itself.

On its status screen the actuator shows **Status:** **“Pulled in”**, **“Pulled out”**, **“Working”** while it moves, or **“Unknown”** — [The sensor status screen](sensor-status-screen.md).

## “Seeding to tramline”

Raised by the seed sensor of a line that should be shut off. See [Seeding alarms](alarms-seeding.md#seeding-to-tramline).


# Dispenser motor alarms

The controller of each electric dispenser motor reports its faults to the panel. The device line names the motor: **Electric motor: #5**. The code of the last fault is on the status screen of the motor, line **Last fault:** — give it to the service. The motor and its settings: [The context menu of a motor](motor-context-menu.md).

| **Alarm text** | **What it means** | **What to check, in this order** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **“Under voltage”** | The supply voltage of the motor controller — for the motor or for its electronics — is too low. | Battery and alternator of the tractor; the power cable and its connectors; the fuse. |
| **“Over voltage”** | The supply voltage is too high. | The charging voltage of the tractor; the power supply of the system against the data sheet. |
| **“Over temperature”** | The controller or its heat sink is too hot. | Let it cool; a dispenser that runs hard; dirt covering the motor. |
| **“Short circuit”** | A short on the motor leads — between them, to ground or to the supply. | The motor cable and connector; the motor. |
| **“Over current”** | The motor draws too much current. | A dispenser that runs hard or is blocked; the motor. |
| **“Motor jammed!”** | The motor is told to turn but does not turn. With **“Rollback when jammed”** at **“Yes”** it first runs back briefly to free itself. | Foreign matter in the dispenser; the drive between motor and dispenser; the motor. |
| **“Device in bootloader!”** | The motor controller is in its update mode and does not run. | Switch the panel and the system off and on. If it stays, call the service. |
| **“FAILURE”** | Any other fault of the controller. | Note **Last fault:** from the status screen and call the service. |

All motors share one more alarm with every device: **“Connection lost”** — [Device does not answer](alarms-any-device.md).


# The context menu of a dispenser motor

On the [Motors screen](motors-screen.md), hold **“MENU”**, select the motor with **“UP”** / **“DOWN”** and press **“MENU”**. What the menu holds depends on the access level and on the seeding mode of the motor.

![The context menu of a seed motor, Agronomist level, machine standing still, Flow mode.](figures/mini-motors-context-menu)

| **Item** | **Level** | **What it does** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **“Information”** | Agronomist | Opens the status screen of the motor. |
| **“Electric motors”** | Service | Opens the service screen of the motors — see [The Motors screen](motors-screen.md). |
| **“Dispenser calibration(weight)”** | Operator | Starts the [calibration by weight](calibrate-motor-weight.md). Shown only while the machine stands still. |
| **“Type of product”** | Agronomist | Which of the three products the motor applies — [Assign a product to a motor](assign-product-to-motor.md). |
| **“Weight, gr”** and **“Rotations”** | Agronomist | Together they describe the dispenser: this weight of product for this number of shaft turns. Set by the calibration; change them by hand only to copy the values of an identical dispenser. |
| **“Minimum, rpm”**, **“Maximum, rpm”** | Agronomist | The permitted shaft speeds. From them the panel works out the travel speeds at which the rate can be applied. The minimum cannot reach the maximum: the panel moves the other value by one step. |
| **“Button input”**, **“Activation signal”** | Agronomist | A push-button on the motor controller to run the motor from the machine during calibration. With **“Button input”** at **“No”**, calibration is run from the panel only. |
| **“Holes in disk”** | Operator | The number of cells in the seed disk; from it the panel works out the disk speed. Only in the **“Precise”** mode. |
| **“Numerator”**, **“Denominator”** | Agronomist | The gear ratio between motor and driven shaft, as the machine builder set it. Change it only after the drive has been rebuilt. |
| **“Rotation direction”** | Agronomist | **“Forward”** or **“Backward”**, as the motor is fitted. |
| **“Rollback when jammed”** | Agronomist | **“Yes”**: when the dispenser jams, the motor runs back briefly to free it. **“No”**: the motor is only stopped. |
| **“Reset to defaults”** | Service | Resets this motor's own settings — see the caution below. |

Further items at the Service level are tools of the service engineer and are not described here.

**Weight items only in “Flow” and “Hybrid”.** **“Dispenser calibration(weight)”**, **“Type of product”**, **“Weight, gr”**, **“Rotations”**, the speed limits and the button items appear only if the motor works in **“Flow”** or **“Hybrid”**. In **“Precise”** the rate comes from the seed sensors, there is nothing to calibrate by weight, and **“Holes in disk”** appears instead.

Taking the motor into or out of control is not in this menu: **“PLUS”** and **“MINUS”** on the Motors screen do that.

> **CAUTION**
>
> **“Reset to defaults” is a reset, not a setting.** **“Holes in disk”**, **“Numerator”**, **“Denominator”**, **“Rotation direction”** and **“Rollback when jammed”** of this motor return to their factory values, and the motor is taken back into control **without asking**. The calibration values, the product type and the speed limits stay as they are.


# Buttons on every screen

The seven buttons are touch areas on the frame: a **short press** is a short touch; a **long press** is a touch held for about half a second. Holding a button never repeats it — one touch, one step. Where the buttons are: [The panel and its seven buttons](front-panel.md).

## Home screen — monitoring

| **Button** | **What it does** |
| --- | --- |
| **“HOME”** | Seeding table. |
| **“HOME”**, long | Locks or unlocks product application (machines with dispenser motors or a liquid pump). One short beep. |
| **“MENU”** | Main menu. |
| **“MENU”**, long | Sensor setup mode. |
| **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”** | First press selects a rate field (it blinks); the next ones raise or lower its set value. |
| **“UP”** / **“DOWN”** | Previous / next rate field. Nothing if there is only one. |
| **“BACK”** | Releases a blinking rate field; otherwise opens the tramline bout menu, if the tramline is on. |
| **“BACK”**, long | While seeding: sets the alarm level from the flow applied — [Set the alarm level](set-the-alarm-level.md). |

## Home screen — sensor setup mode

| **Button** | **What it does** |
| --- | --- |
| **“UP”** / **“DOWN”** | Previous / next device. |
| **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”** | Takes the selected sensor into / out of control, after a question the first time. |
| **“MENU”** | Context menu of the selected device. |
| **“BACK”** | Leaves the mode. |
| **“HOME”** | Leaves the mode and goes to the Seeding table. |

## Seeding table

| **Button** | **What it does** |
| --- | --- |
| **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”** | Next / previous table. |
| **“UP”** / **“DOWN”** | Scroll one row. |
| **“MENU”** | Asks **“Zero readings?”**. |
| **“HOME”** / **“BACK”** | Statistics / home screen. |

## Statistics

| **Button** | **Touch** | **What it does** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **“UP”** / **“DOWN”** | Swipe down / up | Scroll one line. |
| **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”** | Two-finger swipe right / left | Next / previous field. |
| **“MENU”** | Two-finger tap | Menu of the screen. |
| **“HOME”** | Long swipe left | Motors, or the rate control screen. |
| **“BACK”** | — | Home screen. |

## Motors

| **Button** | **What it does** |
| --- | --- |
| **“MENU”**, long | Switches on the selection. |
| **“UP”** / **“DOWN”** | Previous / next motor or actuator. |
| **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”** | Into / out of control, after a question the first time. |
| **“MENU”** | Context menu of the selected motor. |
| **“BACK”** | Leaves the selection; then the home screen. |
| **“HOME”** | Rate control screen. |

## Rate control

| **Button** | **What it does** |
| --- | --- |
| **“HOME”** | Home screen. |
| **“HOME”**, long | Locks or unlocks product application. |
| **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”** | Rate change state; then change the selected target. |
| **“MENU”**, long | Sensor setup state. |
| **“UP”** / **“DOWN”** | Previous / next element in either state. |
| **“MENU”** | Context menu of the selected element; on a product, its motors. |
| **“BACK”** | Leaves the state. Does not leave the screen. |
| Touch and hold | On the settings symbol: main menu. On a product: its motors. On liquid fertilizer: the pump. |

## Menus

| **Button or touch** | **What it does** |
| --- | --- |
| **“UP”** / **“DOWN”** | Move the selection; at the end it jumps to the other end. |
| **“PLUS”** / **“MINUS”** | Change the value of the selected item by one step. |
| **“MENU”** | Enters the item; on a value between **-\[** and **\]+**, opens the number pad. |
| **“BACK”** | One level up. |
| Touch an item | Selects it; a second touch enters it. |

## Number pad

Touch the digits. **“OK”** or **“MENU”** accepts; **“BACK”** cancels. Touch and hold the backspace to clear the number. Nothing else works. See [The number pad](number-pad.md).

## Windows

| **Window** | **Buttons** |
| --- | --- |
| Question | The two buttons named in the window, or touch **“Yes”** / **“No”**. **“BACK”** or a touch outside cancels. |
| Information | Closes by itself, with a touch or with a button. |
| Alarm | **“HOME”** or touch **“Close”** — closes. **“HOME”**, long — closes and returns to the home screen. Other buttons do nothing. |
| Fill the disks | Only **“BACK”**: aborts, or closes when done. |


# Terms used in this manual

| **Term** | **Meaning** |
| --- | --- |
| **Active field** | The field the panel writes its statistics to now, marked **(A)**. [Start a new field](start-a-new-field.md) |
| **Alarm level** | In the **“Flow”** mode: the flow in seeds per second under which a line counts as failing. Drawn as the control line. [Set the alarm level](set-the-alarm-level.md) |
| **Bout** | One pass of the drill across the field. [Set up the tramline rhythm](tramline-rhythm.md) |
| **Context menu** | The menu of one device, opened in the sensor setup mode. [Interface basics](interface-basics.md) |
| **Control line** | The white line across a diagram: the alarm level or the target rate drawn. |
| **Doubles** | Two seeds where one was intended, as a share. |
| **Flow, Hybrid, Precise** | The three control modes of a diagram. **Flow**: seeds per second against an alarm level. **Hybrid**: seeds per metre against a target rate. **Precise**: seeds per metre with skips, doubles and quality. [The section diagram](section-diagram.md) |
| **In control / out of control** | Whether the panel watches a sensor. A sensor out of control raises no alarms. [Take a sensor into or out of control](sensor-in-and-out-of-control.md) |
| **Lock (work pause)** | Product application stopped by hand: motors and pump stand still. [Lock application by hand](lock-application-by-hand.md) |
| **Population** | Seeds per hectare, shown in thousands (**ks/Ha**). Derived from the rate, the working width and the number of rows. |
| **Product** | A material applied by weight, in kg/ha. Up to three: **“Product 1”** to **“Product 3”**. |
| **Profile** | The list of the devices of the machine, set at commissioning. [The profile](profile.md) |
| **Quality (singulation)** | The share of seeds placed singly, as intended — what is left after doubles and skips. |
| **Rate field** | The figures beside a diagram: measured on top, set value below. |
| **Recalculation interval** | The stretch of path (or time without a speed sensor) over which skips, doubles, quality and rate are collected before they are shown anew. Set by **“Recalculation,m”**. A short interval answers quickly but fluctuates; a long one is steadier. |
| **Rhythm** | The number of bouts and which device shuts off on which bout. |
| **Section, line** | One seed or fertilizer line with its own sensor: one column of the diagram. |
| **Sensor setup mode** | The mode in which one device is selected to be switched or set. Hold **“MENU”**. |
| **Skips** | A gap where a seed was intended, as a share. **Not sown** counts the skips over stretches where nothing was sown at all. |
| **Spacing** | The distance between seeds — the rate per metre turned round. |
| **Target rate** | What you set: seeds per metre (**“Hybrid”**, **“Precise”**), kg/ha (products), L/ha (liquid). The population target follows from it and is not meant to be changed during the field. |
| **Tramline** | The lane left unsown for the sprayer. [Next tramline bout](next-tramline-bout.md) |
| **Unknown area** | Area driven while a sensor had no connection or was out of control. |
